78679f76546d9b63: BAGAN SERAI: Police will record statements from six hikers in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing since Aug 29.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the group will be taken to the Gerik district police headquarters for documentation after being brought out from Pos Kemar.

"They will all be allowed to return home after the documentation process is completed. They are also reported to be in good health," he told a press conference at the Kerian police headquarters today.
Asked if the couple committed an offence by bringing their two children on the hike, Mohd Alwi said all four had valid permits.
"There was no issue as the permit included details of their family members," he said.

Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, together with guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before undergoing medical checks at the Pos Kemar health clinic.
The SAR team and victims left Pos Kemar at 8.30am today, arriving at Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding, at 10.20am before proceeding to Gerik police headquarters.
The six began their hike on Aug 29 and were due to exit the forest on Sept 3. A police report was lodged by family members on Sunday after they failed to return as scheduled.– BERNAMA
0069bb43e78c5bb3: IPOH, Sept 8 — The phenomenon of Sungai Perak turning blue was caused by the interaction of several factors, including increased runoff following heavy rain, the presence of mineral particles and changes in water flow conditions, the Perak State Legislative Assembly was told today.

Perak Science, Environment and Green Technology Exco Teh Kok Lim said the finding was based on the Final Report of the Investigative Sampling (IS) Study on Sungai Rui, Gerik, conducted by experts from Scieno TW, a concessionaire appointed by the Department of Environment Malaysia.
He said the report was presented to the Perak State Executive Council on Aug 19.

“Based on the study and analysis, the experts concluded that the phenomenon was caused by the interaction of several factors, particularly increased runoff following heavy rain, the presence of mineral particles and changes in water flow conditions,” he said.

Teh was replying in writing to Kenering assemblyman Mohamad Husairi Arifin, who asked what caused the water in Sungai Perak near the Air Ganda Bridge in Hulu Perak to turn blue in early July, as well as the findings of the investigation and measures taken.
Teh said Hulu Perak was naturally rich in minerals, while heavy rainfall increased runoff, carrying more mineral particles from catchment areas, particularly open areas, into the river system.
He said data obtained by environmental scientist Dr Abd Rani Abdullah showed that rainfall during the phenomenon was almost twice as high as in the preceding period.

“This increased the volume of runoff and carried more mineral particles into the river system. However, rainfall and the presence of minerals alone were not sufficient to produce the colour-changing phenomenon.
“A certain concentration of minerals and suitable water flow conditions had to occur simultaneously,” he said.
Teh said Sungai Rui, being narrower, had a faster current, but the flow slowed when it entered the wider Sungai Perak.

“This allows fine mineral particles to remain suspended and accumulate for a longer period. When these particles interact with light, the scattering and reflection of light causes the water to appear bluish,” he said.
He said the types of minerals present, including copper, iron, aluminium and silica, as well as particle size, also influenced the optical properties and visible colour of the water.
On water quality, Teh said Sungai Perak was currently classified as Class II under the National Water Quality Index (WQI), based on an analysis of more than 30 water quality parameters.

He said the classification meant the river was suitable for uses prescribed under Class II, including recreational activities, fisheries and as a raw water source for conventional treatment before use.

Teh said the state government, through the Department of Environment (DOE), continuously carried out enforcement and inspections on premises subject to the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and its latest amendments.
“This included activities subject to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) requirements and industrial premises governed by the Environmental Quality (Industrial Effluent) Regulations 2009,” he said.
He said the DOE had eight manual monitoring stations and one automated monitoring station along the Sungai Perak Basin.
“Monitoring is carried out by the appointed concessionaire, while river water quality data is monitored online through the Environmental Quality Monitoring Programme.
“Manual monitoring is conducted six times a year,” he said.
Teh said any detected changes or deterioration in water quality would be notified to the DOE through the Notification of Pollution Event Level 1 or Level 2 (NPE 1/NPE 2) mechanism.
He said the early notification would allow the department to promptly identify potential pollution sources and take follow-up action.
On the way forward, Teh said the state government was considering legal, scientific and social aspects, as well as proposals from experts and residents in Hulu Perak.
Among the proposals was a Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) study to determine the pollution load received by Sungai Rui and Sungai Perak and to map or inventory pollution sources.

The state government also proposed establishing a state-level task force led by the Perak Water Resources Management Board to identify and coordinate action among agencies and strengthen collective enforcement.
Other proposals included studying the use of the Mine Rehabilitation Fund to rehabilitate former mining areas.
Teh said the government also planned to identify locations for installing online monitoring systems to obtain real-time data.
“Parameters including pH, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, total suspended solids and conductivity would be monitored as early indicators of abnormalities linked to mining activities,” he said.
He said the state government also planned to establish a Perak-level guideline for mining activities based on benchmarks and best mining practices adopted by leading mining countries.
“Based on these best practices, the state government can direct mining operations to be upgraded from time to time in line with the latest technology,” he said.
48196e1ead944b1f: GEORGE TOWN: Penang International Airport's (PIA) flight operations remain normal despite the haze affecting Penang and other parts of Malaysia, with take-offs and landings so far continuing without disruption.
Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said airport management had informed the state government that the haze had not affected flight operations at the airport.

"Nevertheless, the state government will continue to closely monitor the situation and maintain communication with the airport and airlines, in order to respond to and minimise the impact of haze as well as unforeseen aviation incidents on visitors to Penang and the tourism industry," he said in a statement today.

He said this after leading representatives of the state government and tourism industry in a meeting with newly appointed PIA senior airport manager Ahmad Fikri Samsudin yesterday, which focused on airport operations, capacity, future development and the expansion of international direct flight network.

Wong also noted that there has been no large-scale stranding of Indonesian passengers at PIA following the cancellation of several Penang-Jakarta flights caused by volcanic ash from the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau.

He said affected airlines, including AirAsia, TransNusa and Batik Air, had notified passengers of the cancellations through email, SMS and other communication channels after volcanic ash disrupted operations at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.

Mount Anak Krakatau erupted three times on Tuesday morning as Indonesian authorities continued to monitor its activity, which remains at Level III, or Siaga (Alert), the second-highest level in Indonesia's four-tier volcano alert system.
Meanwhile, Wong said the state government is also preparing for two new international direct routes scheduled to begin in October.

He said Hainan Airlines is scheduled to launch a direct service between Haikou, Hainan, and Penang on Oct 11, while Batik Air is scheduled to begin a direct service between Batam and Penang on Oct 18.

He noted that the Penang state government had in recent years been actively strengthening and deepening its international aviation network by promoting direct air links between Penang and major international cities, with these efforts gradually bearing fruit as international passenger numbers continue to grow.
"The airport recorded 2.64 million international passenger movements from January to July this year, compared with 2.38 million during the same period last year.
"This represents an increase of 264,980 passenger movements, or 11.13 per cent," he said. — BERNAMA

e9b906d1d0b3a5eb: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should act decisively on the police force's call to review and strengthen laws on scams and fraud, including imposing tougher punishment to make the offence a "high-risk, low-reward crime".
Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said he strongly supported Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail's call for existing laws to be reviewed and strengthened.

"The message must be clear: scamming is not a minor offence. It is a serious crime that can destroy lives, wipe out the life savings of victims and cause severe emotional and psychological distress," he said in a statement.
Lee said the reported 500 to 600 calls received daily by the National Scam Response Centre was a clear indication that scams had reached an epidemic level and stronger action was urgently required.

"Scammers are becoming increasingly sophisticated. They exploit technology, manipulate victims psychologically and operate through complex networks involving mule accounts, telecommunications channels, digital platforms and, in some cases, organised criminal syndicates.
"Yet if the punishment does not match the seriousness of the offence, it will not provide an adequate deterrent," he said.
Lee wants the government to consider increasing penalties for major scam-related offences so that the punishment reflects the scale of harm caused to victims.

He also wants heavier punishments for repeat offenders and organised scam syndicates, particularly those deliberately targeting senior citizens, vulnerable individuals and first-time users of digital banking.

"Laws against mule account holders and those who knowingly facilitate scams should also be strengthened, while ensuring innocent people who had been deceived or exploited were treated fairly," he said.
Lee also called for stronger asset-tracing and recovery powers to allow funds obtained through scams to be frozen and recovered as quickly as possible.
He said closer cooperation between police, banks, telecommunications companies, digital platforms and other agencies was needed to detect and disrupt scams before victims suffered financial losses.
"Ensuring faster investigation and prosecution is also important because the certainty and speed of punishment are just as important as the severity of the penalty," he said.
Lee said enforcement alone could not solve the problem, with public awareness and digital literacy needing to be strengthened continuously.
He also urged the public to recognise common scam tactics and adopt a "stop, check and verify" approach before transferring money or disclosing personal information.
He added that banks and technology companies also had an important responsibility to strengthen their safeguards and respond rapidly when suspicious transactions were detected.
"Malaysia must not allow scams to become regarded as an unavoidable consequence of living in a digital society.

"We must make scams a high-risk, low-reward crime for criminals. If the law does not instil fear in those who commit these offences, they will continue to regard scamming as a lucrative business," he said.
It was reported that Khalid had called for amendments to outdated laws and tougher penalties, including the use of the rotan, for online scammers.
He had said existing penalties were too lenient and failed to deter masterminds and members of scam syndicates despite continuous arrests nationwide.
"Arrests are being made continuously nationwide, but the penalties imposed are so minimal that they do not instil fear in criminals," he had said.
He had added that the matter had been raised with the ministry and the government so that legislative changes could be made in line with technological developments and international standards.

c6cc6ec054a4f780: BEIJING, Sept 8 — China’s imports and exports surged in August, helped by a global AI buildout that has fuelled demand for technology products and ahead of an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and US counterpart Donald Trump.

After achieving a historic surplus in 2025, China’s trade has continued to boom this year, thanks largely to heightened overseas demand for semiconductors, computing hardware and other products linked to the artificial intelligence boom.

Exports spiked 25 per cent year-on-year, the General Administration of Customs said, accelerating from July’s 23.9 per cent growth, though the increase was just short of the 25.9 per cent forecast in a Bloomberg survey of economists.
Imports swelled 28.2 per cent, which was faster than July’s 27.5 per cent but less than the 31.0 per cent estimated in the Bloomberg survey.
Strong trade has represented a key lifeline for the Chinese economy in recent months, as domestic activity has been mired in the doldrums.
New growth this year has come from the global AI sector, adding to strengths in other areas including electric vehicles, consumer goods and industrial equipment.
In January through August, the value of China’s exports of computers and related parts surged 49.4 per cent, the customs data showed.
“China continues to rely on the exporters to support the economy,” wrote Zhiwei Zhang, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management.
But soaring surpluses with several key trading partners has also become a political issue, as officials overseas argue that waves of Chinese imports are crowding out local competition.
“The US government made it clear at the G20 meeting that they are concerned about this (trade imbalance) issue,” Zhang wrote.
Shipments to the United States climbed 34.4 per cent year-on-year last month, compared with the 17 per cent increase seen in July.
The latest figures come before Xi and Trump’s expected high-stakes summit in Washington this month.
Last year’s global tariff onslaught unleashed by the US president sparked renewed turmoil in the countries’ trade relationship.
Sky-high levies imposed by Washington and matched by Beijing were tentatively relaxed late last year, after a move by China to severely restrict flows of rare earths to the United States.
Despite the turbulence to global trade last year, China achieved a record US$1.1 trillion surplus.
Strong growth in exports to the European Union, Southeast Asia and Africa helped offset a steep drop in shipments to the United States, which were hit by the tariff war. — AFP
e77736bd90d37af4: Last month, Meta agreed to a settlement with 48 US states over claims that its social media platforms, Facebook and Instagram, violated federal child privacy laws and state consumer protection laws.
Although it did not admit wrongdoing, Meta agreed to pay up to US$18 billion to the states and also make changes to its platforms to improve youth online safety.

These include setting a default daily use limit of two hours for users under 18, restricting notifications during certain hours and hiding reactions (such as "likes") for teenage users. These settings can be turned off by users, but defaulting them to opt-out rather than opt-in is a step in the right direction to reduce engagement and improve online safety.
What implications, if any, does this settlement have for users in Malaysia, where the under-16 social media ban came into effect June 1, 2026?
Three months later, this ban seems to have little impact, as platforms have been given a grace period of six months to set up age verification protocols and remove accounts of users under 16.

It is expected that existing users perceived to be under 16 and new registering users will have to scan government-issued identification to verify their age, similar to verification protocols used by financial institutions. However, evidence from Australia suggests that teenagers are finding ways of getting around age restrictions.
The debate around whether an age-based ban is implementable, enforceable or effective continues, but the Meta settlement reignites a broader online safety discussion.

It shifts the regulatory focus from keeping users away from potential sources of harm and towards requiring platforms to implement safety by design, a principle already embedded in the Online Safety Act 2025.

The Meta settlement implies that a Big Tech company can be held liable for how their product design, such as infinite scrolling and social reward mechanisms, can endanger users. If one company can be held liable, so can others.

On one hand, the settlement allowed Meta to avoid an expensive trial with negative publicity, whatever the outcome. On the other hand, Meta acknowledged what technology policy experts have long been saying: that there are product design decisions and safeguards platform providers can make to improve online safety instead of simply denying responsibility for the content created and shared by individual users on their platforms.

Two significant design features are notably absent from the safety measures Meta is planning to roll out in the US: customised feeds and infinite scroll. Customised feeds use algorithmic recommendations to fine-tune content shown to users, intending to align content with user preferences.

While these can introduce new content to users, over-customisation can lead to echo chambers reinforcing a particular worldview or state of mind, increasing confirmation bias and potentially reinforcing misinformation.
Furthermore, customised feeds are designed to increase engagement, for example by showing shocking content that is more addictive. In extreme cases, this can lead to radicalisation.

Infinite scroll automatically loads the next few pieces of content when a user scrolls to the bottom of the page. This creates a continuous stream of content that encourages prolonged engagement by offering a constant supply of new information and dopamine hits.
By removing stopping points, infinite scroll can encourage addictive behaviour, affecting mental health as well as reducing attention spans.

These features are relatively recent innovations of the attention economy. Earlier versions of social media feeds were user-curated, where content from creators and sources chosen by the user appeared chronologically with limited algorithmic recommendations.

Feeds also had natural stopping points, determined by the number of posts, followers or timespan. It is a simple technical matter to bring back these earlier designs, which would return some control to the user.

Platform providers are unlikely to want to curtail these design features that maximise prolonged engagements and thus profits. Nonetheless, the Meta settlement shows that collective action supported by evidence can apply enough pressure to yield results.
Malaysia's current online safety legislation permits regulators to demand more accountability from platforms. Policymakers looking to improve online safety should take note.
RACHEL GONG Associate Director of Research, Khazanah Research Institute

850c31445d44e402: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Cooperation and consensus among members of the Cabinet are, as a whole, at a good level, thereby contributing to the country’s political stability, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this had enabled the government to plan and implement the country’s development agenda based on clear policies and a stable political environment.

“True, we cannot deny that our performance has been commendable because we have clear policies, political stability and cooperation within the Cabinet, although sometimes on social media it is a little different.

“But in terms of cooperation, we generally have good consensus and this provides an indication of stability and allows us to plan for the country,” he said when delivering his address during his meeting with the staff of the Ministry of Plantations and Commodities here today.
Anwar said the existing stability must be leveraged by the government to continue planning and implementing policies that benefit the country and the people as a whole.
At the same time, the Prime Minister reminded all parties not to become complacent with the achievements attained, but instead to continue striving to improve the government’s performance.

He said commendable achievements should not cause the government to “become complacent and bask in the comfort of success”, but should instead serve as an encouragement to continue working hard for the national interest.

“It’s true, it cannot be denied, our performance is commendable because of our clear policies, our political stability and the cooperation within the ministries, although sometimes on social media things are a little different,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said that economic growth in the second quarter of this year also recorded a better performance than expected despite facing challenges.

Malaysia is reported to have continued to record stronger-than-expected performance for three consecutive quarters, growing by six per cent in the second quarter of 2026 compared with 5.4 per cent recorded in the previous quarter.
This was the strongest second-quarter performance outside the pandemic period since 2014.

The second quarter 2026 performance brought the country’s first-half 2026 growth to 5.7 per cent, thus placing the Malaysian economy on a solid footing to achieve the government’s projected growth of between 4.0 per cent and 5.0 per cent for 2026. — Bernama
08fbecdfb54ba841: JOHOR BARU: No Johor government officials have been implicated in the corruption probe involving a housing committee chairman.

State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the Johor government would leave the case entirely to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and the legal process.
He said the investigation did not involve anyone in the state administration, whether executive councillors or government officers.

"I do not want to comment on the merits of the case under investigation and leave it entirely to the MACC and the legal process to conduct a transparent, professional investigation in accordance with the law," he told the New Straits Times when asked for comment.

Yesterday, Johor MACC arrested a housing committee chairman in his 40s over allegations of soliciting about RM4,000 from each of 400 applicants for government housing lots, involving an estimated RM1.6 million.
The suspect is also alleged to have misused a housing committee's bank account and withdrawn funds using fake invoices.
Jafni urged all parties not to speculate or link this case to the Johor administration.
He added that he would not tolerate anyone exploiting, cheating or abusing their position for personal gain in matters involving public housing.
"Those entrusted with such responsibility must not betray the hopes and hardships of the people who want to own a home," he said.
He also urged the public to deal only through official channels and not make payments to individuals or parties requesting money in connection with housing matters.
"Any request for payment should be reported immediately to the authorities.
"The state government remains committed to completing 30,000 affordable homes by the end of this year, with more than 21,000 units completed and handed over to Johoreans," he said.
The state's housing agenda was aimed at expanding access to affordable homes while ensuring the process remained organised, transparent and based on integrity, he added.
"In matters involving public housing, trust must be protected. The rights of the people must never be traded."
86421f17ab71ae2d: SEPANG: Pakatan Harapan is prepared for all possibilities in the upcoming Melaka election, including contesting solo without cooperation from Barisan Nasional.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the coalition has yet to receive any official decision regarding cooperation or seat distribution with BN for the state polls.
Asked whether PH is ready to contest without BN, he said the coalition is fully prepared to face such a scenario.
He said discussions with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh have so far only taken place online and have not entered formal negotiations.

"As of today, there is nothing official yet. If there is cooperation, we proceed with it. If not, we will see whether we face each other or not," Amirudin told reporters at NCT Smart Industrial City today.
"This matter was raised, and they expressed readiness to discuss. We agreed to talk, but no specific date or time has been set."
Media reports previously quoted Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, hinting that the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly could be announced by the end of this month.
Speaking at an event in Sungai Udang yesterday, Ab Rauf hinted that the assembly dissolution would take place within "two Fridays".
Amirudin, however, noted that the statement remains speculative, as the final decision on dissolving the state assembly rests with the Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri.
"How many Fridays does two Fridays mean? If one Friday has passed, then it becomes three Fridays. We shall see, as these are all hints," he said.
"Regardless, it is his prerogative as Chief Minister, subject to the approval of the Yang di-Pertua Negeri."
Amirudin added that PH is stepping up preparations for various contingencies given the tight timeline, including facing a different political landscape compared with previous state elections.
He jokingly added that the worst-case scenario would be not contesting at all, saying a political party should not exist if it does not contest elections.
fec53983ea364820: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The future of education for the Malay and Bumiputera communities must move beyond quotas towards greater self-reliance and resilience.

Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the success of the communities should instead be measured by their ability to excel in critical fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), develop new technologies and own intellectual property.

“The measure is not only the number of students entering university, but how many can think critically, master STEM, build global companies and lead world-class institutions,” he said when officiating the Malay Education Convention 2026 here today.

Zambry said that to achieve this goal, the country’s education ecosystem needed to move beyond simply providing access towards improving quality, building competencies, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing from technology use to technology ownership.

He said Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) should no longer be viewed as a second choice, but as a key pathway for developing national talent and producing highly skilled technicians and problem-solving experts.

Addressing the narrative of Bumiputera dependency, Zambry said affirmative policies remained relevant as long as structural imbalances persisted, but their ultimate objective must be to empower the Bumiputera community to achieve excellence and become independent.
“Malay and Bumiputera education cannot forever be built on the narrative that ‘we need to be helped because we are weak’.
“The narrative of the future must be: ‘We are given the opportunity to become strong, stand on our own, lead and help others’,” he said.

Zambry also stressed that mastery of the Malay language was important as a language of knowledge and identity, while proficiency in English and other languages was essential to competing globally without compromising integrity.

“In the pursuit of global excellence, we must never lose our identity and values. Education must produce not only intelligent people, but individuals of good character, integrity and the moral courage to lead,” he said.
On the convention, which is a continuation of the Bumiputera Education Congress held on May 1, Zambry said it would culminate in the formulation of a comprehensive resolution.
He said the resolution would subsequently be submitted to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi for consideration and further policy action by the government. — Bernama
522c9de8edad4740: CLARENCE TOWN: Australian firefighters say they are on alert as temperatures in the southern hemisphere begin to pick up, following a devastating fire season in Europe.
Australia is already experiencing a strong El Nino weather event that typically brings with it hotter, drier weather, and an increased risk of wildfires.

“We're concerned this year that we'll see increased fire risk (versus) prior years,” said Trent Curtin, head of the New South Wales Rural Fire Service, the world’s largest volunteer firefighting force.
Large parts of Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent, endured sweltering summers, leaving vegetation tinder-dry and fuelling severe wildfires.
Britain had its hottest summer since records began, with Italy’s the warmest for 75 years.
“We're seeing some extraordinary conditions in the northern hemisphere at the moment,” Curtin said.
“They're experiencing fires that they haven't seen for a couple of decades or maybe never seen before.”
Australia has a long history of fighting wildfires, including the 2019 to 2020 Black Summer blazes that destroyed an area the size of Turkey and killed 33 people.
Authorities frequently conduct hazard reduction burns, where sections of forest are burnt in a controlled manner to reduce the spread of wildfires should they happen.

“For this year we're alert but not alarmed. We’re conscious of the fact that the seasonal outlook is expecting a busier than usual fire season – conditions will be quite dry, hot,” said Alex Capararo, a sector commander for the Forestry Corporation of New South Wales, which manages state-owned land, as he led a hazard reduction burn around three hours north of Sydney.
Peak fire danger season usually starts in mid-October in northern New South Wales and in December in southern parts of the state, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.
00398ec6772e49ae: MONTREAL: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, as a trade war between the North American neighbours heats up.

The announced duties of 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent apply to $27.6 billion (US$20 billion) in imports from the United States, covering steel and aluminium products as well as dairy goods like cheese. But Canada removed some seafood products from the initial list.

Ottawa's pushback comes weeks after US President Donald Trump imposed 50-per cent tariffs on a similar value of Canadian products, over what Washington deemed as "discriminatory treatment" against US alcohol, automobile and dairy industries.
The US tariffs hit items like hockey sticks and cement, impacting about 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the United States.
On Monday, Trump threatened to block sales of Canada's Bombardier Aviation in the United States, unless the Quebec-based plane maker moves manufacturing to the US.
"No more selling Bombardier in the United States!" Trump posted in all caps on his Truth Social platform, though he did not specify how he would achieve a sales halt.
Thousands of Bombardier aircraft currently operate in US airlines' domestic fleets.

In a statement Monday, the aerospace company touted its creation of "tens of thousands of jobs across the United States," with "direct employment" in more than 20 states, including Kansas, Texas, Arizona and California.
The company also noted that it spends over US$2.5 billion annually with suppliers, and said its supply chain is "made up of approximately 2,800 American companies across 47 states."
"Bombardier values its great partnership with American companies and its US employees," the company's statement said.
US tariffs pose a modestly negative risk to Canada's overall economy, but analysts note that they have a sharper impact on Central Canada's manufacturing sector.
Negotiations between both sides broke down August 21 after days of meetings in Washington, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney saying he decided to suspend the trade talks.

At the time, Carney said the Trump administration's terms were ultimately unacceptable, adding that US negotiators had introduced restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries at the eleventh hour.
US officials also made unacceptable "threats" to the French language and "Quebec culture," he added, referencing the French-speaking province in eastern Canada.
But Trump's top trade official Jamieson Greer later noted that the US government is aware that French language protections are sensitive and important.
"This is not something where we push hard, or condition, or red-line," he told Canadian public broadcaster CBC last month.
- WAR OF WORDS -
Ottawa and Washington have not resumed negotiations since, and have continued trading barbs.

Asked if both sides were in a trade war, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week (Aug 31) that he did not think one could be in a tit-for-tat fight with a country that is 13 times larger.

"We're not at war with Canada," Bessent said on the sidelines of a G20 finance leaders' meeting. "How are we going to be at war with Canada? They're going to take their two set submarines from the Edmonton Mall and sic them on us?"
He was referring to a former attraction at a shopping centre in the Alberta province.
Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth separately appeared to mock the physical appearance of a Canadian soldier on social media.
Carney said a day later that the remarks were "beneath their office," adding that this was "not constructive."
He said both sides can have discussions "when the Americans stop doing memes" and start being serious.
Trump also signed an order in August to rename Lake Ontario, on the border with Canada, as "Lake America."
This has sparked anger in Canada, amid a broader wave of patriotism triggered by Trump's hostility.
At the start of his second presidency, Trump also ordered the Gulf of Mexico be renamed the Gulf of America. He has made claims that Canada should become the 51st US state as well.

Although Carney is backed by Canadian public opinion, his country remains reliant on its neighbour. Nearly 60 per cent of Canada's imports come from the United States and about 70 per cent of its exports go to the US market.

a28b684479216684: MONTREAL, Sept 8 — Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, as a trade war between the North American neighbours heats up.

The announced duties of 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent apply to C$27.6 billion (RM80 billion) in imports from the United States, covering steel and aluminium products as well as dairy goods like cheese. But Canada removed some seafood products from the initial list.

Ottawa’s pushback comes weeks after US President Donald Trump imposed 50-per cent tariffs on a similar value of Canadian products, over what Washington deemed as “discriminatory treatment” against US alcohol, automobile and dairy industries.
The US tariffs hit items like hockey sticks and cement, impacting about 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the United States.
Yesterday, Trump threatened to block sales of Canada’s Bombardier Aviation in the United States, unless the Quebec-based plane maker moves manufacturing to the US.
“No more selling Bombardier in the United States!” Trump posted in all caps on his Truth Social platform, though he did not specify how he would achieve a sales halt.
Thousands of Bombardier aircraft currently operate in US airlines’ domestic fleets.

In a statement Monday, the aerospace company touted its creation of “tens of thousands of jobs across the United States,” with “direct employment” in more than 20 states, including Kansas, Texas, Arizona and California.
The company also noted that it spends over US$2.5 billion annually with suppliers, and said its supply chain is “made up of approximately 2,800 American companies across 47 states.”
“Bombardier values its great partnership with American companies and its US employees,” the company’s statement said.
US tariffs pose a modestly negative risk to Canada’s overall economy, but analysts note that they have a sharper impact on Central Canada’s manufacturing sector.
Negotiations between both sides broke down August 21 after days of meetings in Washington, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney saying he decided to suspend the trade talks.

At the time, Carney said the Trump administration’s terms were ultimately unacceptable, adding that US negotiators had introduced restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries at the eleventh hour.
US officials also made unacceptable “threats” to the French language and “Quebec culture,” he added, referencing the French-speaking province in eastern Canada.
But Trump’s top trade official Jamieson Greer later noted that the US government is aware that French language protections are sensitive and important.
“This is not something where we push hard, or condition, or red-line,” he told Canadian public broadcaster CBC last month.
War of words
Ottawa and Washington have not resumed negotiations since, and have continued trading barbs.

Asked if both sides were in a trade war, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week (Aug 31) that he did not think one could be in a tit-for-tat fight with a country that is 13 times larger.

“We’re not at war with Canada,” Bessent said on the sidelines of a G20 finance leaders’ meeting. “How are we going to be at war with Canada? They’re going to take their two set submarines from the Edmonton Mall and sic them on us?”
He was referring to a former attraction at a shopping center in the Alberta province.
Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth separately appeared to mock the physical appearance of a Canadian soldier on social media.
Carney said a day later that the remarks were “beneath their office,” adding that this was “not constructive.”
He said both sides can have discussions “when the Americans stop doing memes” and start being serious.
Trump also signed an order in August to rename Lake Ontario, on the border with Canada, as “Lake America.”
This has sparked anger in Canada, amid a broader wave of patriotism triggered by Trump’s hostility.
At the start of his second presidency, Trump also ordered the Gulf of Mexico be renamed the Gulf of America. He has made claims that Canada should become the 51st US state as well.

Although Carney is backed by Canadian public opinion, his country remains reliant on its neighbour. Nearly 60 per cent of Canada’s imports come from the United States and about 70 per cent of its exports go to the US market.
To help businesses and workers, Canada’s government has unveiled an aid package of C$7.5 billion. — AFP

aa6b61830e5b27b3: GEORGE TOWN: Malaysia is assessing the potential role of nuclear energy in its future energy mix as rising demand from artificial intelligence, data centres, and advanced industries puts greater pressure on the nation's power needs.

Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Malaysia is conducting assessments and preparatory work, but stressed that no decision has been made on whether to adopt nuclear power.

"We are undertaking the necessary assessments and preparatory work on the potential role of nuclear energy in our future energy mix," he said at the 9th Engineering, Science and Technology Congress (ESTCON 2026) at the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre today.
Speaking at a press conference later, Chang clarified that the government is currently focused on building the capabilities needed to support any future decision on nuclear energy.
He said preparations under the Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry cover three key areas: technology development, talent development, and regulatory framework development.
Other aspects will be considered by the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (PETRA), he added.
Chang emphasised that these preparations do not mean the government has decided to adopt nuclear energy, but are necessary to ensure Malaysia is prepared should it eventually proceed.
He said any government decision on whether to adopt nuclear energy will only be made beyond 2030.

Earlier in his speech, Chang noted that Malaysia's growing strength in semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and the digital economy is driving unprecedented demand for energy and digital infrastructure.
He said the country's longer-term energy requirements must be assessed comprehensively as AI, cloud computing, and hyperscale data centres expand.

"AI cannot flourish without reliable and sustainable energy systems," he said, adding that energy security, industrial competitiveness, digital transformation, and climate resilience are increasingly interconnected.
Chang said Malaysia is also strengthening its capabilities in strategic and emerging technologies, including nuclear technology, as it seeks to achieve greater technological self-reliance.
488734ceba6c2206: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia menjadi tuan rumah Mesyuarat Menteri Kesihatan Asean (AHMM) buat kali pertama dalam tempoh 22 tahun, dengan tumpuan untuk memastikan perbincangan mengenai kerjasama kesihatan serantau diterjemahkan kepada tindakan nyata.

AHMM ke-17 dan mesyuarat berkaitan berlangsung di Kuala Lumpur dari 7 hingga 11 Sept, menghimpunkan menteri kesihatan, pegawai kanan serta rakan antarabangsa dengan tema “Asean Sihat: Bersama Ke Arah Sistem Kesihatan Saksama dan Bersedia Menghadapi Masa Depan”.
Malaysia kali terakhir menjadi tuan rumah mesyuarat dwitahunan itu pada 2004 dan mempengerusikan pertemuan kali ini, manakala Myanmar menjadi timbalan pengerusi.

Menurut Kementerian Kesihatan, mesyuarat itu menandakan fasa baharu dalam diplomasi kesihatan Malaysia dengan penekanan lebih besar terhadap pelaksanaan dasar dan inisiatif yang mampu memberi hasil nyata.

Aktivis kesihatan awam Dr Sean Thum berkata kepentingan AHMM terletak pada keupayaan Asean menyelaras tindakan terhadap ancaman kesihatan yang sukar ditangani secara berkesan oleh sesebuah negara secara bersendirian.

Katanya, kerjasama serantau boleh membantu mewujudkan piawaian bersama, menyelaras pemantauan, memudahkan perkongsian maklumat, menggabungkan kepakaran dan perolehan serta membangunkan protokol serantau.
“Apabila kita menggabungkan keupayaan, kita berpotensi melakukan perkara yang sukar atau kurang berkesan jika dilaksanakan oleh sesebuah negara secara bersendirian,” katanya.
Pentas diplomasi lebih luas

Pertemuan tahun ini turut menyaksikan Mesyuarat Menteri Kesihatan Asean-AS dan Asean-Jepun diadakan buat kali pertama, sekali gus memperluaskan perbincangan melangkaui kerjasama sesama negara anggota Asean.
Pertemuan peringkat menteri turut diadakan bersama China, Korea Selatan dan Pertubuhan Kesihatan Sedunia (WHO).
Kementerian Kesihatan berkata pertemuan itu akan memperkukuh kerjasama teknikal serta membuka lebih banyak peluang pelaburan dalam sektor kesihatan serantau.
Mesyuarat itu berlangsung ketika keperluan terhadap kerjasama rentas sempadan semakin meningkat, terutama dalam aspek keselamatan kesihatan, penyakit baharu dan daya tahan sistem penjagaan kesihatan.

Thum berkata kekuatan kolektif Asean juga boleh dimanfaatkan bagi perolehan dan rantaian bekalan serantau, pengeluaran ubat-ubatan dan vaksin, kerjasama penyelidikan serta perkongsian kepakaran teknikal yang terhad.
Daripada dasar kepada tindakan
Antara pencapaian utama minggu ini ialah pelancaran Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026–2030, yang akan menjadi hala tuju kesihatan rantau ini bagi tempoh lima tahun akan datang.

Satu lagi keutamaan ialah mempercepatkan pelaksanaan Asean Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases bagi meningkatkan kesiapsiagaan rantau ini menghadapi pandemik pada masa depan serta ancaman penyakit baharu.
Mesyuarat itu turut membincangkan pendekatan bersepadu untuk menangani beban berganda penyakit berjangkit dan tidak berjangkit di Asean.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Galen Centre Azrul Khalib berkata AHMM berpotensi mempengaruhi dasar negara menerusi piawaian bersama, komitmen serantau, kerjasama teknikal, perkongsian data dan akauntabiliti politik.
Malaysia turut menggunakan mesyuarat itu untuk memajukan perbincangan mengenai beberapa bidang khusus dalam kerjasama serantau.

Antaranya penyediaan Deklarasi Penyakit Jarang Jumpa Asean, inisiatif kesihatan mata MySPECS, pendekatan berasaskan pemahaman tingkah laku, kerjasama kesihatan paru-paru serantau, penyelidikan rawatan penyakit terabai serta kawal selia peranti perubatan.
Inisiatif itu mencerminkan usaha lebih luas untuk membawa isu yang sudah ditangani di peringkat negara kepada kerjasama lebih menyeluruh di seluruh Asean.
Mengapa kerjasama serantau penting
Thum berkata kekuatan Asean terletak pada keupayaan menggabungkan kelebihan negara anggotanya, berbanding setiap negara menangani ancaman kesihatan bersama secara berasingan.
Beliau memberi contoh jerebu rentas sempadan, dengan asap serta kesannya terhadap kesihatan tidak terhenti di sempadan sesebuah negara.

Katanya, kerjasama serantau lebih kukuh boleh menyokong pemantauan kesihatan bersama, perkongsian maklumat masa nyata serta tindak balas kesihatan awam yang diselaraskan apabila jerebu menjejaskan beberapa negara.

Azrul pula berkata pandemik Covid-19 memberi satu lagi pengajaran apabila ia menunjukkan betapa perkongsian maklumat, rantaian bekalan perubatan dan kapasiti penjagaan kesihatan boleh menjadi kelemahan kritikal ketika berdepan krisis serantau.

Katanya, kerjasama lebih kukuh boleh membantu negara mengesan wabak lebih awal, berkongsi maklumat dengan lebih pantas serta meningkatkan kapasiti serantau dalam penyediaan ubat-ubatan, vaksin dan tindak balas kecemasan.

Kementerian Kesihatan berkata inisiatif yang dibawa menerusi AHMM bertujuan memastikan kerjasama serantau memberi manfaat nyata kepada lebih 670 juta penduduk Asean, selaras dengan penekanan Malaysia Madani terhadap sistem kesihatan yang inklusif dan mampan.
Thum berkata Asean yang lebih sihat akhirnya akan menjadikan setiap negara anggotanya lebih selamat.
71b0bd47c2a08255: HONOLULU: Residents of Kauai were warned to watch for tornadoes late Monday as Hurricane Lowell edged toward the westernmost Hawaiian islands in the US Pacific island chain, the National Weather Service said.
"Conditions are favourable for tornadoes in and close to the watch area" of Kauai, including the city of Lihue, NWS officials said.
The core of Lowell was expected to pass near or just west of Niihau late Monday or early Tuesday, the National Hurricane Center said in a bulletin at 5pm (0300 GMT).
"Dangerous conditions are expected for Niihau, Kauai and Oahu, with flash flooding, damaging waves and high winds expected from Lowell," NHC said.
The centre warned that the combination of a storm surge and tide would flood normally dry areas near the coast in Kauai and Niihau.
A tropical storm warning was also issued for the island of Oahu, where Honolulu is located.
The storm was expected to dump 4-8 inches of rain on Kauai, with 3-8 inches of rain forecast for the Big Island.
The storm was about 370km southwest of Honolulu and moving north-northeast, the centre said.
Lowell, which was packing maximum sustained winds of 175km per hour, was expected to gradually weaken over the next several days.
The storm briefly reached Category 5 strength earlier this week.
Hawaii is still recovering from the impacts of Hurricane Lala, which grazed the southern part of the Big Island last month, bringing destructive winds and flash floods.

Lowell is one of two storms in the Pacific Ocean right now, where a near-record-strength El Nino climate episode warms the waters. Tropical Storm Marie, about 745 miles southwest of San Diego, was moving west away from land.
El Nino is the warming phase of a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific known as the El Nino-Southern Oscillation. It comes along every two to seven years.
The oscillating climate pattern promotes hurricane formation in the tropical Pacific while decreasing their likelihood in the Atlantic.
Climate change increases El Nino's global weather impacts.--AFP
c6eb68eab000dc04: GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has called for a transparent investigation into the Penang ferry collision that injured 21 passengers.

CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the Sept 1 collision between the ferry and chemical tanker MV Mekar Jaya near the Sultan Abdul Halim Ferry Terminal could have resulted in a far more serious incident.
He welcomed the Penang Port Commission's (PPC) investigation into the collision within Penang Port limits and urged authorities to take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence.

Mohideen said the incident raised questions over the effectiveness of the port's Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS), which was introduced in June to enhance safety, efficiency, and sustainability.
"The VTMS can monitor vessel movements through systems such as radar and the Automatic Identification System (AIS)," Mohideen said today.

"Records from these systems could establish the vessels' positions, speeds, headings, and movements in the minutes leading up to the collision, helping determine whether they were on a collision course and when the danger should have become apparent."
Mohideen urged the PPC to establish whether the VTMS was monitoring both vessels when the incident occurred and determine what information was available to its operators before the collision.
He also called for an investigation into whether warnings or communications were issued to either vessel.
However, Mohideen stressed that the VTMS should not be viewed as a substitute for the responsibilities of vessel masters and crews.
"Responsibility for navigation and collision avoidance ultimately remains with the vessels' crew," he added.
He said the investigation should examine the actions of both vessels, as well as whether existing traffic-management arrangements, including the VTMS, had functioned effectively.
Calling for the investigation findings to be made public, Mohideen said the public has a right to know the cause of the collision and whether safety measures were adequate.

"The findings should identify whether failures in navigation, communication, traffic management, or other procedures contributed to the incident, and those responsible must be held accountable," he said.
b91da7f1c31a9f6a: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan memberikan lanjutan tempoh kepada pihak pendakwaan untuk mengesan bekas pembantu penyelidik Yusoff Rawther dan menyerahkan sendiri notis rayuan kepadanya berhubung pembebasannya daripada pertuduhan pengedaran dadah dan pemilikan senjata api tiruan.
Hakim Azman Abdullah menetapkan 4 Nov untuk pihak pendakwaan memaklumkan kepada mahkamah sama ada notis itu berjaya diserahkan.

Peguam Yusoff, Rafique Rashid Ali, berkata anak guamnya tidak membantah rayuan itu didengar secara dalam talian.

Azman berkata mahkamah tidak boleh mendengar rayuan itu tanpa kehadiran Yusoff melainkan pihak pendakwaan terlebih dahulu berusaha menyerahkan notis tersebut, seperti yang dikehendaki oleh undang-undang.
Beliau berkata mahkamah juga terikat dengan duluan undang-undang yang menghendaki notis rayuan diserahkan sendiri kepada Yusoff, yang merupakan responden dalam kes itu.

Semakan dengan rekod Jabatan Imigresen juga mendapati Yusoff telah meninggalkan Malaysia pada Jun tahun lalu.
Rafique berkata anak guamnya sedang memohon suaka di UK dan tidak akan kembali ke Malaysia.

Hakim Jamil Hussin yang kini telah bersara memutuskan bahawa pihak pendakwaan gagal membuktikan Yusoff mempunyai pengetahuan, pemilikan atau kawalan ke atas dadah dan pistol tiruan tersebut.
Yusoff didakwa mengedar 305g kanabis yang didakwa ditemui dalam kenderaannya di luar surau polis Kuala Lumpur pada 6 Sept 2024. Dadah itu didakwa dibungkus dalam beg plastik hitam.
Beliau juga didakwa memiliki dua pistol tiruan di luar Kondominium Senada di Jalan Bukit Kiara pada 9.25 pagi hari sama.
Pembelaan Yusoff sepanjang perbicaraan ialah dadah dan pistol tiruan itu sengaja diletakkan untuk menuduh beliau adalah pemilikannya.
22490f2c2a49d0c8: PETALING JAYA: Local companies of all sizes need to accelerate automation in operations and production as the future supply of foreign workers is unlikely to match current levels, says investment, trade and industry minister Johari Ghani.

"We want many companies, regardless of size, whether micro, small or medium, to understand how important it is to bring automation into operations and production as soon as possible," he told reporters after officiating the Women, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy Forum.
He said foreign workers were brought in to do dirty, dangerous and difficult jobs, not to replace local workers, Bernama reported.
Johari said employers who claim that locals do not want to work should reconsider their offers.
"If they are offered the minimum wage, maybe they do not want it as they don't see the economic value. Our people are willing to go to Singapore to work because there is economic value," he said.

The forum brought together perspectives from government, academia, industry and entrepreneurship to discuss the role of women in the AI era, particularly the question of who creates and owns value as AI increasingly shapes the future economy.
c4917a28636bbdb8: BEIJING, Sept 8 — China began collecting “deposits” on imports of a key chipmaking chemical from Japan today after it said a probe found evidence of dumping that harmed Beijing’s domestic industry.
The Chinese commerce ministry announced in January an anti-dumping investigation into dichlorosilane imported from Japan — a major global supplier of the chemical used to manufacture semiconductors.

The probe came at a time of heightened diplomatic tensions between the Asian giants after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi suggested Tokyo may intervene in an attack on the island of Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its territory.

The Chinese commerce ministry said on Monday that “preliminary evidence showed the investigated imports from Japan were involved in dumping, and the domestic dichlorosilane industry suffered substantial damage”.
As a result, the ministry said it would implement “temporary anti-dumping measures in the form of a security deposit” beginning Tuesday.
Japanese firms must pay the extra fee, calculated using an assigned deposit collection rate, to China’s customs authority.
All Japanese firms are subject to a rate of 99.2 per cent, with the exception of Tokyo-based Denal Silane, which was given a rate of 80.8 per cent.
A spokesman for Japanese chemical conglomerate Shin-Etsu Chemical told AFP the firm was studying the measure.
He declined to discuss financial details about the exports of the product, but said “it represents a very small portion of our business (and) should have no material impact on our overall business”.
Minoru Kihara, the Japanese government’s chief cabinet secretary, told his daily media briefing that Tokyo would “appropriately respond to China’s export control measures”.
“Japan has lodged a strong protest and is formally requesting that these measures be withdrawn,” he added.
The Chinese commerce ministry did not say how long the imported chemical would be subject to deposits, or when it would announce a final ruling. — AFP
57ce90cc0f5b058a: BEIJING: China's imports and exports surged in August, official data showed on Tuesday, helped by a global AI buildout that has fuelled demand for the country's technology products.
Exports spiked 25% year-on-year, the General Administration of Customs (GAC) said, accelerating slightly from July's growth of 23.9%.
The increase fell just short of a Bloomberg forecast of 25.9%.
Imports swelled 28.2% year-on-year, which was faster than July's 27.5 % but short of Bloomberg's forecast of 31.0%.

After achieving a historic trade surplus in 2025, China's trade has continued to boom this year, due largely to heightened overseas demand for semiconductors, computing hardware and other products linked to the artificial intelligence boom.
In January through August, the value of China's exports of computers and related parts surged 49.4%, the GAC data showed.
Shipments to the US climbed 34.4 % year-on-year last month, compared with the 17% increase seen in July.
The latest figures come before an expected high-stakes summit in Washington this month between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

24e3a277c4c2c316: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia is hosting the Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) for the first time in 22 years, with a push to turn regional health cooperation policy discussions towards concrete action.

The 17th AHMM and related meetings, held in Kuala Lumpur from Sept 7 to 11, bring together health ministers, senior officials and international partners under the theme "Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems".
Malaysia last hosted the biennial meeting in 2004 and is chairing this year’s gathering, with Myanmar as vice-chair.
According to the health ministry, the meeting marks a new phase in Malaysia's health diplomacy, with greater emphasis on implementing policies and initiatives that can deliver tangible results.
Public health advocate Dr Sean Thum said the significance of the AHMM lay in Asean's ability to coordinate responses to health threats that individual countries could not effectively tackle alone.
He said regional cooperation could help set common standards, coordinate surveillance, facilitate information-sharing, pool expertise and procurement, and develop regional protocols.
"When we pool our capabilities, we can potentially do things that are difficult or inefficient for an individual country," he said.
A bigger diplomatic stage
This year’s gathering also marks the first Asean-US and Asean-Japan health ministers’ meetings, expanding discussions beyond cooperation among Asean member states.
Ministerial engagements are also being held with China, South Korea and the World Health Organization.
The health ministry said these engagements would deepen technical cooperation and expand opportunities for regional health investment.
The meetings come amid an increasing need for cross-border cooperation in matters of health security, emerging diseases and resilient healthcare systems.

Thum said Asean's collective scale could also support regional procurement and supply chains, pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturing, research collaboration and the sharing of scarce technical expertise.
From policy to action
One of the main milestones this week is the launch of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026–2030, which will serve as the region’s health road map for the next five years.

Another key priority is advancing the operationalisation of the Asean Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases, aimed at strengthening the region's preparedness for future pandemics and emerging health threats.
The meeting will also look at an integrated approach to Asean's dual burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases.
Galen Centre CEO Azrul Khalib said AHMM could shape national policy through common standards, regional commitments, technical cooperation, shared data and political accountability.
Malaysia is also using the meeting to advance discussions on several specific areas of regional cooperation.

These include the drafting of an Asean Rare Diseases Declaration, the MySPECS eye-health initiative, behavioural insights, regional lung-health cooperation, research into treatments for neglected diseases and medical-device regulation.
The initiatives reflect a wider effort to take issues already being tackled at the national level and build cooperation around them across Asean.
Why regional scale matters
Thum said Asean's strength lay in combining the capabilities of its member states rather than having countries tackle common health threats separately.
He gave the example of transboundary haze, saying that smoke and its health effects do not stop at national borders.
Stronger regional cooperation could support shared health surveillance, real-time information-sharing and coordinated public health responses when haze affects several countries, he said.

Azrul, meanwhile, said the Covid-19 pandemic offered another lesson, exposing how quickly information sharing, medical supply chains and healthcare capacity could become critical vulnerabilities during a regional crisis.
Stronger cooperation could help countries detect outbreaks earlier, share information faster and build greater regional capacity for medicines, vaccines and emergency response, he said.

The health ministry said the initiatives being advanced at AHMM are intended to translate regional cooperation into tangible benefits for more than 670 million people across Asean, in line with Malaysia Madani emphasis on inclusive and sustainable health systems.
Thum concluded that "a healthier Asean will lead to safer individual countries".

5a7e146049a9f2bf: KUALA LUMPUR: Women's success in the digital economy must extend beyond online sales to becoming suppliers, manufacturers and exporters.

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said greater participation by women was essential to expanding the economy, with their businesses growing to supply products needed by other industries.

"If our economy is now worth RM2 trillion and we want it to reach perhaps RM3 trillion or RM4 trillion in the next 10 years, participation must come not just from men, but from all Malaysians, particularly women," he said at the opening of the Voices of Her 2026 Forum at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
Johari said women who expanded beyond online sales would strengthen their position in economic value chains and generate a wider multiplier effect as other businesses used their products.
"When she expands to become a supplier, vendor, manufacturer, exporter or business partner through the merger of two small companies, she has progressed much further.
"She has become part of the economic value chain," he said.
He said the government had provided substantial assistance to help women start businesses, use digital platforms and market their products.

Johari said his ministry and its agencies would help businesses of all sizes adopt automation and artificial intelligence (AI), including for product redesign, to improve competitiveness, speed up production and increase the value of their products.

He said Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) can also help businesses reach overseas markets by introducing their products abroad and connecting potential buyers with local manufacturers online.

"We will provide as much assistance as possible to help businesses adopt these technologies so that products made by Malaysians become more competitive, can be produced faster and have higher added value," he added.
cbdc59524cf82179: JOHOR BARU: A contractor was fined RM20,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to using forged documents in a bid to secure RM5 million worth of Felda road and drainage upgrading projects three years ago.
Wan Shahrinizam Wan Ibrahim, 50, pleaded guilty to two charges of dishonestly using forged documents as genuine before Judge N. Kanageswari.
The court ordered him to serve three months in jail for each charge if he failed to pay the fines.

The first charge involved a bank statement dated from November 2022 to January 2023, which was allegedly falsified and submitted through Felda's e-procurement system as part of an application to undertake road resurfacing and drainage upgrading works at Felda Ciku 3, Gua Musang, Kelantan, worth RM5 million.

The second charge involved a forged letter of acceptance for a tender for resurfacing works using premix and repairs to the drainage system along Jalan Parit Yaani and Parit Botak, Batu Pahat, as well as related works.
Wan Shahrinizam was alleged to have instructed an officer to upload the document into the same e-procurement system as part of the application.
Both offences were committed at a premises in Jalan Watan, Taman Desa 3, Parit Setongkat, Muar, in February 2023.
He was charged under Section 471 of the Penal Code, which provides for punishment under Section 465 and carries a maximum two-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
The prosecution accepted a representation on another related charge to be taken into consideration under Section 171A of the Criminal Procedure Code.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Irna Julieza Maaras prosecuted, while lawyers Azalea Nazihah and Muhammad Denial represented Wan Shahrinizam.

3c7c2ee72e0f924c: KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of UUE Holdings Bhd surged more than nine per cent in morning trade today, amid heavy trading activity.

58b7f4dabf84a40e: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has given the prosecution a further extension to locate former research assistant Yusoff Rawther and personally serve him with a notice of appeal against his acquittal of drug trafficking and possession of imitation firearms charges.
Justice Azman Abdullah fixed Nov 4 for the prosecution to update the court on whether the notice has been served.
Justices Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and K Muniandy were also on the bench for the appeal today.
Deputy public prosecutor Asnawi Abu Hanipah told the bench that police had sent a request to Interpol in Manchester on July 22 to locate Yusoff and serve the notice on him.
"We are waiting for a response from Interpol," he said, asking for an extension of up to two months to update the court on efforts to locate Yusoff and serve the notice.
Yusoff’s counsel, Rafique Rashid Ali, said his client did not object to the appeal being heard online.
The lawyer previously told the court that he did not know Yusoff’s exact location in the UK, although he remained in contact with his client through Zoom.
Azman said the court could not hear the appeal in Yusoff’s absence unless the prosecution first attempted to serve the notice, as required by law.
He said the court was also bound by legal precedent requiring personal service of the notice of appeal on Yusoff, the respondent in the case.
On June 15, Azman, Muniandy and Justice Radzi Abdul Hamid granted the prosecution more time to locate Yusoff.

Checks with the immigration department showed that Yusoff left Malaysia in June last year. Rafique subsequently told the court that his client was seeking asylum in the UK and would not be returning to Malaysia.
On June 12 last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court acquitted Yusoff of both charges without calling for his defence.
Judge Jamil Hussin, who has since retired, ruled that the prosecution failed to prove that Yusoff had knowledge, custody and control of the drugs and imitation pistols.

Yusoff was charged with trafficking 305g of cannabis allegedly found in his vehicle outside the Kuala Lumpur police surau at about 10.15am on Sept 6, 2024. The drugs were allegedly wrapped in a black plastic bag.
He was also charged with possessing two imitation pistols outside Senada Condominium in Jalan Bukit Kiara at about 9.25am that same day.
Yusoff maintained throughout the trial that the drugs and imitation pistols were planted to frame him.
6a6359a25350bdec: PORTO, Sept 8 — Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said yesterday finding form early in the season “was not easy” for his World Cup players ahead of the club’s Champions League opener at Porto.
“I think it’s correct that you see these kinds of players that they start to be tired,” Maresca said at the Dragao Stadium before Tuesday’s match.
Maresca was responding to remarks by Erling Haaland posted on the striker’s his YouTube channel earlier in the day.
The Norwegian has three goals in three league matches but did not play in warm up games, following Norway’s run to the World Cup quarterfinals.
“The new season started and I didn’t even have a pre-season. I normally have a bit of pre-season but this time, just nothing,” said Haaland.
“The physical side will come, if you manage to stay injury free, but you need to be sharp mentally as well, and that’s not easy.
“We need to have that eager feeling to go back but we don’t because there is no time to properly stay away from football because there are so many games and the season is longer.
“I’m not complaining because it’s still a positive thing that you get to play football throughout the whole year and live off it.
“But sometimes we need a break as well.
“I never played a World Cup so I don’t know how it is.”
“It’s not easy for them, it’s not easy for Erling, it’s not easy for most of the players that they continue to play for their international team,” said the coach.
“It’s correct to give them some rest that can be one game out or can be one week away depends a little bit in which moment we are.
“To be focused on the day by day makes it very complicated to think where we can be in February, March, April in terms of expectation.
“The most important thing is to see that we are improving game after game.” — AFP

f728eeded76b8051: SINGAPORE: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slowed at the start of this week, after Iran threatened on Monday to retaliate for any new US attacks.

Goldman Sachs also raised its Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude oil price forecasts for December 2026 and 2027, as it expects shipping disruptions in the Middle East to persist into next year.

1bca4cab2ba90a1c: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said there was room to improve the existing Asean mechanism for tackling transboundary haze.
He stressed that the issue required more serious attention given its impact on public health.

“I think the Asean ministers must seriously look at it because this is affecting lives, particularly children and babies,” he told reporters when met at the Plantation and Commodities Ministry monthly assembly here today.
Anwar was responding to questions on whether the current Asean mechanism on transboundary haze was sufficient and whether stronger enforcement was needed.
He said the recurring impact of haze on neighbouring countries showed the need to assess whether existing regional mechanisms were sufficiently effective.
“The Asean ministers have to seriously look at this,” he said.
When asked on action taken against alleged perpetrators, Anwar said those were merely allegations as fires detected were mainly forest fires.
“Most of the fires that we detected were forest fires,” he said.
Anwar acknowledged that Malaysia had companies operating in Indonesia and would allow Indonesian authorities to take action if Malaysian firms were found to be involved.
“If there are Malaysian companies involved, we give room for Indonesia to take action.
“We certainly will not defend them,” he said.
Anwar’s remarks come as the region continues to grapple with the recurring problem of transboundary haze, which can affect air quality and public health across national borders.
ff7ca2bd3518ada5: NEW YORK, Sept 8 — Coco Gauff bested rising US star Iva Jovic yesterday to reach the quarter-finals of the US Open for the first time since winning the title three years ago.
Gauff, seeded fourth this year, beat the 14th-seeded Jovic 6-1, 6-4 in 80 minutes.

The match marked a rare instance in which two-time Grand Slam champion Gauff, still only 22, faced a younger American in the 18-year-old Jovic, who pushed Gauff in the second set after being routed in the first.
“She plays beyond her years,” Gauff said. “I’m looking to many more battles out here.”
Gauff said she served “really well” and called the win, along with a second-round victory over Spain’s Paula Badosa, her best matches so far this year.
Gauff has yet to lose a set so far in New York and has pointed to an improved serve as a source of confidence.
“I’m able to rely on a lot of different things to win points in many different ways, and I think that gives me a confidence,” Gauff said after yesterday’s match.
Broken to open the contest, Gauff reeled off six straight games to take the first set.
Gauff said some of the marathon rallies left her breathless, but she came out on top of them more often than not.
Jovic picked up the pace in the second set, rushing the net behind strong shots to keep Gauff on the defensive.
Their net exchanges won loud applause from fans, and Gauff finished the match with a surprise serve-and-volley ambush, landing a volley that Jovic couldn’t put back in play.
Gauff will next face French Open champion and fifth-seeded Mirra Andreeva of Russia in the quarter-finals. Gauff has won all five of their prior meetings.

Despite the strong record against Andreeva, Gauff noted that most of the matches have been close. In their last contest, Gauff defeated Andreeva 6-4 in the third set in the quarter-finals of Rome, shortly before Andreeva’s Paris triumph.

“She’s obviously in a different mindset now, at the top of the game, coming off a Grand Slam win,” Gauff said of the Russian. “So I expect her to approach the match completely differently from in the past.” — AFP
12d6ec35fb3f08f4: PETALING JAYA: Selangor FC’s application to stay the sanctions imposed by the Football Association of Malaysia (FAM), including an order for the club to play behind closed doors due to the rowdy behaviour of its supporters, has been rejected.

eaaade80d07c937f: MANILA: Philippine jobless rate climbed to the highest in four years as fresh graduates sought work in an economy that slowed due to a corruption scandal and the global oil shock.

July unemployment rate stood at 6%, the statistics agency reported on Tuesday. That matches the rate in June 2022, when the economy was recovering from the coronavirus pandemic. The capital region of Metro Manila logged the highest jobless rate of 8.2%, partly due to the influx of new graduates.

More than 3.7 million people joined the labour market from a year ago and not all of them were absorbed by employers, National Statistician Dennis Mapa told a briefing. More than a million of them were aged 15-24 years, who transitioned from schooling, he said.

The latest jobs data comes as the administration of president Ferdinand Marcos Jr is already under pressure by rising cost of living as the Philippines grapples with the highest inflation in Southeast Asia and companies wary of hiring more people amid slower economic expansion.

Philippine economic growth sharply slowed to 2.3% in the second quarter. Businesses have also become more pessimistic, with overall confidence index down to -20.3% in July from zero in June, according to the latest central bank survey.
The central bank said that over the next 12 months, fewer firms indicated plans to hire additional workers amid expectations of softer growth and elevated inflation.

“More Filipinos are participating in the labour market, which means that we need to intensify efforts to attract investments, especially those that create quality jobs,” Economic planning secretary Arsenio Balisacan said in a statement.
af073c2fb0329687: SANAA: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi media Ansarollah said Tuesday that the rebels hit targets in Saudi Arabia, as they press an offensive to seize territory near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Days of fighting near the Red Sea coast have left more than 300 people dead and displaced hundreds of families as the Houthis try to capture land bordering the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

The strait forms the southern entrance to the Red Sea, a shipping artery that has become vital for Saudi oil exports amid Teheran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the US-Iran war on Iran.
Almasirah quoted Hassan Saboula, director-general of civil defence in Jawf province, saying that Monday's prison strike killed 11 people and left 20 inmates missing under the rubble.

bf36a849edbfe04c: KUALA LUMPUR: United States Assistant Secretary for Educational and Cultural Affairs Cate Dillon paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives for Malaysia's peace and independence during a wreath-laying ceremony at Tugu Negara.
