5d54e9602c81cc98: KUALA LUMPUR: Asean remains favoured over China and South Asia for economic opportunities, according to the EU-Asean Business Council (EU-ABC) survey.
Many are looking to expand within the region, even as global disruption weakens business confidence, the survey stated.
This puts Asean in the pole position for the fourth consecutive year.
"Trade and investment sentiment has also recovered from last year, and the region is gaining ground as a supply-chain diversification hub," it said.
EU-ABC executive director Chris Humphrey said the global situation has certainly proved challenging, but European businesses have shown a firm commitment to Asean.
"Investment appetite has increased, with most companies planning to expand within the region.
"That tells us Asean remains central to business growth, even as companies rethink their investment and operational strategies," said Humphrey.
Around 150 European business leaders participated in the survey, a yearly exercise that takes stock of business sentiment towards Southeast Asia.
The survey found that nearly four in five (78 per cent) surveyed EU business representatives expect trade and investment in Asean to increase over the next five years (up from 71 per cent in 2025).

It also cited that Asean ranks as the region offering the strongest economic opportunities for the fourth consecutive year, with 61 per cent choosing it over other major emerging economies, including China and South Asia, up from 56 per cent in 2025.
"Seventy-eight per cent (of respondents) plan to expand business operations in at least one Asean market. Vietnam and Indonesia remain the top two destinations," it noted.
However, the survey said US tariff policy uncertainty remains a key concern, with 81 per cent saying it has weakened business confidence in Asean.
While the expansion share has declined from 87 per cent in 2025, plans to contract operations have also fallen from 39 per cent in 2025 to 29 per cent this year.
Plans for expansion are concentrated within Asean's six biggest markets, led by Vietnam, with 64 per cent of respondents looking to expand in the country.
Indonesia ranked second at 57 per cent, followed by both Malaysia and Thailand at 49 per cent, and Singapore and the Philippines at 44 per cent and 43 per cent respectively.
"With both expansion and contraction plans declining, the findings point more towards a stabilising European presence, rather than withdrawal from the region.
"This is further supported by stronger investment expectations and an improved perception of economic opportunities," said Humphrey.
Although business sentiment was broadly positive, respondents were clear that trade and investment conditions in Asean remain challenging.
Growing non-tariff barriers and regulatory unpredictability were ranked as the biggest constraints on trade and investment and similarly cited as the greatest pain points in supply chain usage.

b68741a68f0f9bb4: IPOH, Sept 8 — Congestion at government hospitals in Perak is partly caused by elderly patients arriving with family members and coming earlier than their scheduled appointments, the State Legislative Assembly told today.

Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman A. Sivanesan said elderly patients were usually accompanied by their children or other family members, while some also arrived early in the belief that they could see doctors sooner.
“Sometimes when we give them appointments, they do not come alone. When elderly parents or senior citizens come, they usually come with their children or someone to accompany them.
“They also tend to arrive early because they think that if they come early, they can see the doctor earlier. This cause congestion inside the hospitals as well at the parking area,” he said.

Sivanesan was replying to additional questions by Selinsing assemblyman Sallehuddin Abdullah who asked on issues of patient need to wait longer at government hospital and also whether government hospital bed capacity was sufficient to meet the state’s growing population and increasing chronic diseases.
Sivanesan said doctors also had other duties, including ward rounds, before attending to patients, which could contribute to longer waiting times as patients arrive early than the scheduled time.
However, he said patients generally remained satisfied with the treatment provided by doctors despite having to wait.

Sivanesan also contrasted the situation with private hospitals, where patients using medical insurance may sometimes have to wait longer for approval from their insurance companies before being discharged.

He said negotiations between private hospitals and insurance companies over treatment charges could sometimes take several hours, while patients could leave government hospitals immediately after being discharged.
“We don’t have such issues in the government hospitals. When discharge, patients can leave immediately,” he said.

He said the state Health Department had taken several measures to reduce congestion, including allowing patients to make appointments by telephone to collect their medication directly from the pharmacy.
“We are also implementing a service where, for a certain charge, medication can be delivered directly to the patient’s home,” he said.
On bed capacity, Sivanesan said Perak had 15 government hospitals with about 6,000 beds, of which approximately 5,600 were operational, leaving around 400 beds vacant.
He said there were also 96 intensive care unit (ICU) beds, with about 75 currently operational.

Sivanesan acknowledged that there could be temporary shortages during unexpected disease outbreaks or major emergencies, such as accidents involving schoolchildren, which could require patients to be transferred to other hospitals.
“Sometimes we may face such problems, but so far, we have not received complaints from hospitals or health facilities regarding a lack of beds,” he said.
He added that the state also had 89 health clinics and more than 180 other health facilities, with the government continuing to prioritise patients’ needs and improve healthcare services.
c12bef1f98f245e3: NEW YORK: Doubts over Elena Rybakina's fitness lingered until the eve of the US Open and the Kazakh said she was amazed by her progress from an ankle injury after reaching the quarter-finals on Monday to edge closer to the world number one ranking.

The second seed arrived in New York without having played since retiring from her Cincinnati Open quarter-final against Iga Swiatek last month but has pieced together a superb run to storm into the last eight without dropping a set.

She took apart two-times winner Naomi Osaka in the fourth round to set up a meeting with Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, and another victory will help her leapfrog Aryna Sabalenka and secure top spot in the rankings next week.
"My preparation wasn't that great. I didn't play for seven days and I couldn't do much in the gym movement-wise, so we had to really go day by day," Rybakina told reporters.
"It's amazing progress. I'm really glad how everything worked out. We didn't even know if I'm going to be able to play or not. I have a great team. Also, a good doctor on the phone all the time.
"I can't say that all the matches were amazing, but today it was one of the best matches I played."
Rybakina had never previously reached the quarter-finals of the US Open and she said her latest run had improved her relationship with the tournament and New York.
"Well, now it's getting better and better," she added.
"I usually don't perform that well. Now I feel like this year it's the best for now out of all the years that I've played here.
"I like New York and it's an amazing city. For me, maybe just for two, three weeks, because afterwards it might be too much. I really love the crowd here.
"I enjoy playing in stadiums like this."

11b2029c9d66ca61: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has warned against the unsustainable trajectory of public spending, stressing that the government cannot indefinitely expand allocations while managing the growing cost of subsidies.

Speaking at the Plantation and Commodities Ministry’s monthly assembly today, Anwar called for greater fiscal discipline, arguing that the government must move away from the habit of addressing every crisis simply by increasing funds.

“There is a need for greater discipline in managing public expenditure. We cannot continue responding to every problem simply by increasing allocations, particularly when the cost of subsidies remained high,” Anwar said.
“We have already paid RM40 billion in subsidies. This is not a small amount.”
The PM stressed that rising expenditure must be coupled with measurable outcome, questioning the long-term viability of the current spending model.
“If we keep increasing (spending), how long can we continue?”
Anwar maintained that the government’s primary responsibility is to ensure that public spending produces meaningful results for the people, rather than merely increasing budget lines year after year.
His remarks comes amid demands for increased allocations from some ministries at a time the government is grappling with the significant fiscal burden of direct subsidies
On Aug 30, Anwar noted that petrol and diesel subsidies, which benefit a wide spectrum of income groups including the M40 and T20, cost the government approximately RM40 billion.

Despite this fiscal pressure, the government continues to balance austerity with social welfare. Anwar recently announced the restoration of the basic entitlement for the Budi Madani RON95 programme, increasing the limit from 200 to 300 litres a month to support over 16 million users.
Today, Anwar acknowledged that many Malaysians continue to struggle with the cost of living, admitting that the government does not assume all problems have been solved.
He noted that while six immediate measures were introduced last month, further steps are necessary to ease household pressures.

These considerations are expected to be central to the formulation of Budget 2027, as the administration weighs the need for targeted assistance against the imperative of maintaining a stable fiscal position.
c73873650a86d53d: PETALING JAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan menaikkan hukuman penjara enam tahun enam bulan terhadap seorang wanita kerana menikam teman lelakinya sehingga maut kepada 12 tahun selepas memutuskan hukuman asal tidak menggambarkan keseriusan kesalahan itu.

Panel tiga hakim yang terdiri daripada Hakim Zaini Mazlan, Wong Kian Kheong dan Evrol Mariette Peters sebulat suara membenarkan rayuan pendakwaan terhadap hukuman yang dijatuhkan Mahkamah Tinggi Johor Bahru.

Peters, yang menyampaikan alasan penghakiman penuh, berkata Mahkamah Tinggi 'terlalu bersimpati' terhadap tertuduh dengan memberikan penekanan berlebihan terhadap usianya, sementara gagal memberikan pertimbangan sewajarnya terhadap keseriusan pembunuhan itu.
Mahkamah Rayuan bersidang di Johor Bahru minggu ini.
Wanita itu, yang hanya dikenal pasti sebagai Shy bagi melindungi identitinya, berusia 19 tahun ketika kejadian di sebuah bilik hotel pada 20 Sept 2022.
Dia dan teman lelakinya yang berusia 29 tahun, yang menjalin hubungan selama hampir setahun, mendaftar masuk ke sebuah hotel berhampiran Jalan Austin Heights.
Menurut dokumen mahkamah, pertengkaran tercetus selepas lelaki itu meminta hubungan seks. Shy menolak dengan mengatakan bahawa dia sedang haid.
Lelaki itu kemudian mengugutnya dengan sebilah pisau, menyebabkan dia bergelut dengannya untuk mendapatkan senjata tersebut. Semasa bergelut, Shy menikam lelaki itu beberapa kali di dada.
Bedah siasat mendapati 28 kecederaan, dengan beberapa luka tikaman di dada disenaraikan sebagai punca kematian.
Shy menyerah diri kepada polis dan pada mulanya didakwa atas kesalahan membunuh di bawah Seksyen 302 Kanun Keseksaan.

Susulan representasi peguamnya, pihak pendakwaan bersetuju untuk mengurangkan pertuduhan kepada menyebabkan kematian tanpa niat membunuh di bawah Seksyen 304(a). Dia mengaku bersalah terhadap pertuduhan yang dipinda itu, dan Mahkamah Tinggi menjatuhkan hukuman penjara enam tahun enam bulan.

Dalam membenarkan rayuan pendakwaan, Peters berkata hukuman maksimum di bawah Seksyen 304(a) ialah 30 tahun. Katanya, Parlimen menaikkan hukuman maksimum daripada 20 tahun pada 2007, yang mencerminkan keseriusan kesalahan itu.
Peters berkata Mahkamah Tinggi juga terkhilaf apabila menganggap kehilangan status pesalah muda tertuduh sebagai faktor yang meringankan hukuman.
Shay berusia 22 tahun ketika disabitkan dan oleh itu tidak lagi termasuk dalam takrif pesalah muda, kata mahkamah.
Mahkamah turut menolak cadangan bahawa keadaan pergaduhan itu mengurangkan keseriusan kesalahan dengan ketara.
“Ini bukan satu tikaman yang dilakukan secara impulsif. Pelbagai kecederaan itu menunjukkan serangan ganas yang berterusan,” kata Peters.
Mahkamah mengakui usia muda Shy, pengakuan bersalah, penyesalan, tiada rekod jenayah dan keadaan psikiatrinya sebagai faktor yang meringankan hukuman.
Bagaimanapun, mahkamah berkata faktor-faktor itu perlu diseimbangkan dengan 28 kecederaan, penggunaan pisau, sasaran pada bahagian dada dan kehilangan nyawa seorang lelaki berusia 29 tahun.
Mahkamah memutuskan bahawa hukuman penjara 12 tahun adalah setimpal dan perlu demi kepentingan awam, serta memerintahkan hukuman itu berkuat kuasa dari tarikh Shy ditangkap.
Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Noor Farhana Adham hadir bagi pihak pendakwaan manakala K S Pang mewakili wanita itu.
a6a7f3bcebba5611: PETALING JAYA: Majlis Belia Wilayah Persekutuan (MBWP) mahu membangunkan ekosistem industri kreatif belia di peringkat Asean menerusi kerjasama dengan Gerakan Ekonomi Kreatif Nasional (GeKrafs).

Kerjasama itu dimeterai menerusi memorandum persefahaman (MoU) antara MBWP dan GeKrafs Malaysia, disaksikan Duta Besar Republik Indonesia ke Malaysia Mohammad Iman Hascarya Kusumo serta Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Perbadanan Kemajuan Filem Nasional Malaysia (FINAS) Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib.
Presiden MBWP Khairul Rizam Abu Samah berkata kerjasama itu bertujuan mewujudkan jaringan belia Malaysia-Indonesia yang lebih tersusun, khususnya dalam industri kreatif, teknologi dan keusahawanan.

Menurutnya, inisiatif itu bukan sekadar pertukaran idea, malah dirangka untuk membuka peluang ekonomi baharu kepada belia Malaysia menerusi akses kepada pasaran, pelaburan, teknologi dan rangkaian industri di peringkat serantau serta global.

“Matlamat utama adalah membentuk ekosistem industri kreatif anak muda di peringkat Asean serta mewujudkan ruang penciptaan ekonomi anak muda Malaysia di peringkat global dalam bidang industri kreatif,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Khairul Rizam berkata kerjasama itu turut memberi tumpuan kepada pembangunan bakat menerusi program pemecutan, kelas induk teknikal, kem latihan, webinar pengewangan harta intelek serta bengkel media digital.
Program berkenaan bertujuan meningkatkan kemahiran dan keupayaan profesional usahawan kreatif muda.

MBWP dan GeKrafs juga akan membangunkan platform pemadanan perniagaan, ekspo, hackathon, pameran seni digital serta pertandingan idea kreatif bagi menghubungkan pencipta muda dengan pelabur dan pemain industri dari Malaysia, Indonesia serta negara Asean lain.
Ketua DLPN GeKrafs Malaysia Rika Amelia Rush berkata kerjasama dua hala itu akan menggabungkan rangkaian profesional muda MBWP dengan ekosistem pengamal industri kreatif GeKrafs.
Katanya, jaringan itu akan memperluas perkongsian ilmu, akses pasaran dan pelaksanaan inisiatif digital bersama.

Kerjasama berkenaan turut dirangkaikan dengan Ekraf Talk, Mini Expo dan Business Matching Ekonomi Kreatif Indonesia-Malaysia yang mengetengahkan peluang dalam ekonomi kreatif, pelaburan, perdagangan, teknologi dan digitalisasi.
Program itu turut merangkumi inovasi, pembangunan perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS) serta keusahawanan.

Rika berkata inisiatif itu diharap menjadi platform berterusan untuk melahirkan pemimpin industri kreatif Asean yang mampu mencipta peluang ekonomi, menembusi pasaran antarabangsa serta mengangkat karya dan bakat belia Malaysia ke peringkat global.
a6bcb0e7d8427f90: NEW YORK, Sept 8 — Alexander Blockx beat Francisco Cerundolo in four sets yesterday to become the first Belgian man ever to reach the US Open quarter-finals.
The 21-year-old Blockx, seeded 28th in his Flushing Meadows debut, out-lasted 24th-seeded Cerundolo 6-3, 4-6, 7-5, 7-5.

Blockx, who upset fifth-seeded Flavio Cobolli in the third round, backed up that win with a determined performance during which he received “magical medication” from the doctor to combat a “sharp pain in my rib.
“I was just holding on to be honest,” Blockx said. “Even though I won that first set 6-3, it could have been the other way round.”
Later, Blockx told reporters he might have retired had he lost the third set.
“I was really close to retiring, to be honest,” he said. “I was just hanging in there, but I think if I would have lost the third set, I think the chances were really high of me retiring.”
“Even before the match I was already under medication, and during the match I had medication. So if you feel that much pain while having a lot of medication, that’s not a good sign.”
But “eventually it got better,” he said. “It would have been a shame if I would have retired and then it got better afterwards. I was just lucky.”
The win marks the latest stepping stone for Blockx, who began the year outside the top 100 and had to qualify for the Australian Open.
After splitting the first two sets, Blockx and Cerundolo stood level at 5-5 when the Belgian fell behind 0-40 on his serve.
Blockx worked his way back with big serves and booming strokes, holding serve and breaking Cerundolo in the next game to take the third set.
A tight fourth set went with serve until Blockx gained the winning break in the final game, falling to the ground in delight when a shot from the Argentine landed out.
“This morning I stepped onto this court for the first time to warm up and that felt unreal, so to play a match here and win a match here is even crazier,” Blockx said
Blockx next faces Russian Karen Khachanov, who edged 14th-seeded American Learner Tien in five sets, 7-5, 4-6, 6-7 (6/8)), 6-1, 6-4.
A former US Open semi-finalist, Khachanov beat third-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime in the second round. — AFP
453f93c00bc06fa4: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian palm oil futures extended gains for a third straight session on Tuesday, supported by stronger rival edible oils and crude oil prices.
The benchmark palm oil contract for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained RM21, or 0.42 per cent, to RM4,999 (US$1,235.85) a metric ton in early trade.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract rose 0.42 per cent, while its palm oil contract added 1.67 per cent. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.59 per cent.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Oil prices extended gains as risks of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East grew after Iran threatened to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets, heightening worries over supply disruption.
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
The ringgit, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.05 per cent against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

India's aggressive vegetable-oil buying has led to congestion at major ports, delaying vessel unloading by as much as 10 days as shore tanks fill and refiners struggle to clear incoming cargo, industry officials told Reuters.
Palm oil may revisit its August 21 high of RM5,031 per metric ton, as the uptrend from RM4,614 could have resumed, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.

The yen surged on Tuesday, while Asian markets struggled for direction as a mixed batch of regional economic data and fresh Iranian threats in the Persian Gulf drove oil prices and bond yields higher.
3adb9be1e291fd26: IPOH: The RM6.25 billion Ipoh Sentral project will not involve the acquisition of land belonging to individuals, said Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.

1c43ea03974d948c: PETALING JAYA: The Court of Appeal has increased a woman’s prison sentence for fatally stabbing her boyfriend in a hotel room from six years and six months to 12 years, ruling that the original sentence did not reflect the gravity of the offence.

A three-member bench comprising Justices Zaini Mazlan, Wong Kian Kheong and Evrol Mariette Peters unanimously allowed the prosecution’s appeal against the sentence imposed by the Johor Bahru High Court.

Peters, who delivered the broad grounds of judgment, said the High Court had been "over-sympathetic" towards the accused by placing excessive emphasis on her age while failing to give sufficient weight to the seriousness of the killing.
The Court of Appeal is sitting in Johor Bahru this week.
The woman, identified only as Shy to protect her identity, was 19 at the time of the incident on Sept 20, 2022.
She and her 29-year-old boyfriend, with whom she had been in a relationship for almost a year, checked into a hotel near Jalan Austin Heights.
According to court documents, an argument broke out after the man demanded sex. Shy refused, saying she was menstruating.
He then threatened her with a knife, prompting her to struggle with him for the weapon. During the struggle, she stabbed him multiple times in the chest.
An autopsy found 28 injuries, with multiple stab wounds to the chest listed as the cause of death.
Shy surrendered to the police and was initially charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

Following representations by her lawyer, the prosecution agreed to reduce the charge to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304(a). She pleaded guilty to the amended charge, and the High Court sentenced her to six years and six months in jail.

In allowing the prosecution’s appeal, the Court of Appeal noted that the maximum sentence under Section 304(a) was 30 years. Parliament increased the maximum from 20 years in 2007, reflecting the seriousness with which such offences were to be treated, it said.
Peters said the High Court also erred in treating Shy’s loss of youthful offender status as a mitigating factor.
She was 22 when convicted and therefore no longer fell within the statutory definition of a youthful offender, the court said.
The appellate court also rejected the suggestion that the circumstances of the struggle significantly reduced the seriousness of the offence.
"This was not a single impulsive stab. The multiple injuries demonstrate a sustained violent attack," Peters said.
The court acknowledged Shy’s youth, guilty plea, remorse, lack of previous convictions and psychiatric condition as mitigating factors.
However, it said these had to be balanced against the 28 injuries, the use of a knife, the targeting of the chest and the loss of a 29-year-old man’s life.
Peters drew on Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice to underline the need for a proportionate sentence.
"She is young, remorseful and traumatised, and for that, she deserves leniency. But she owes a debt, not to Shylock, but to the memory of the deceased and his grieving family," she said.
The court held that 12 years was proportionate and necessary in the public interest, and ordered the sentence to take effect from the date of Shy’s arrest.
Deputy public prosecutor Noor Farhana Adham appeared for the prosecution while K S Pang represented the woman.
5d5725c7017cf25f: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged government administrators to fast-track the implementation of public programmes, insisting that success must be measured by tangible benefits to the people rather than mere spending figures.
Speaking at the Plantation and Commodities Ministry’s monthly assembly today, Anwar warned that while Malaysia’s economic performance remains encouraging, the administration must resist complacency.
“We must not be happy and feel satisfied. Firstly, our implementation must be faster, bigger,” he said.
The prime minister highlighted a persistent disconnect between high-level government planning and the actual experiences of citizens on the ground.
He cited the neglected state of Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) housing as a prime example of this failure, noting that some homes and projects have gone years without essential attention.

“We have to work quickly. In relation to housing, example toilets — these are things that should concern us,” Anwar stated, adding that the government must adopt a citizen-centric lens to truly understand the hardships faced by the people.

On the agro-commodity sector, Anwar said that a total of RM425.65 million in measures is being considered under Budget 2027. This package includes RM280.03 million for oil palm replanting by smallholders and RM100 million for the Smallholder Farm Road Programme.
Touching on the issue of infrastructure, the PM stressed that functionality must take precedence over aesthetics.
“The roads don’t need to be sophisticated. They don’t need to be something elaborate. What is important is that they can be used to transport the produce,” he said.

Further allocations under consideration include RM28.57 million for the Agro-Commodity Sector Disaster and Disease Control Fund and RM17.05 million to strengthen downstream agro-commodity entrepreneurs.
Anwar then reminded officials that increasing allocations is meaningless without efficient execution.
He cautioned that positive macroeconomic indicators must be matched by stronger implementation to ensure that the benefits reach the grassroots.
“We have achieved such good performance. That is why I want to remind you: don’t be contented,” he said.
8d0ac8ad3915033c: MUMBAI: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries is set to return to India's rupee bond market after nearly three years, five merchant bankers told Reuters late on Monday, with what would be the largest single-tranche fundraising by a rated firm since November 2023.

The oil-to-telecom conglomerate plans to raise 125 billion rupees (US$1.32 billion) through a sale of five-year notes, at an annual coupon of 7.47 per cent, and is set to invite bids from investors in the week ending September 18, according to bankers.
The issue would be RIL's first rupee bond offering since November 2023, when it raised 200 billion rupees in what was the largest local-currency debt sale by an Indian non-financial company.
The bankers requested anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to the media, while the company did not immediately reply to a Reuters email seeking comment outside normal business hours.
A sharp decline in yields on up to five-year bonds locally has made such funding cheaper than dollar debt sales, the bankers added.
The five-year government bond yield has plunged 33 basis points since the start of June, mainly backed by mammoth dollar inflows under the central bank's subsidised schemes.
Flows led by those in the non-resident dollar deposit scheme pulled down local yields, while higher US Treasury rates lifted the cost of dollar funding for Indian borrowers.
Large private banks are acting as arrangers for the deal, and are also set to partly subscribe to these bonds, the bankers added.
Meanwhile, the company is also mulling a 10-year bond issue and is in discussions with bankers and investors.
e5fbaa00f6e56893: GEORGE TOWN: There has been no mass stranding of Indonesian passengers at Penang International Airport (PIA) after the cancellation of several flights to and from Jakarta following the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau in Indonesia, says Penang executive councillor Wong Hon Wai.
Wong, the state tourism and creative economy committee chairman, said affected airlines included AirAsia, TransNusa and Batik Air, which operate direct flights between Jakarta and Penang.
He said the airlines notified passengers early through email, SMS and other communication channels.

"As a result, there has been no large-scale stranding of Indonesian passengers at PIA," he said in a statement after a meeting between state government representatives and PIA’s newly appointed senior airport manager, Ahmad Fikri, yesterday.
Six Penang-Jakarta flights were cancelled on Sept 6 after the temporary closure of Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport due to volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau.
The disruption reportedly affected 6,279 passengers on 59 departing flights at KLIA.

Wong also said the airport management informed him that the severe haze affecting Penang and other parts of the country had not disrupted flight operations at PIA, with flight take-offs and landings continuing as usual.
However, he said the state government would continue to monitor the situation and maintain communication with the airport and airlines.
"(This is) in order to respond to and minimise the impact of haze as well as unforeseen aviation incidents on visitors to Penang and the tourism industry," he said.
08387bba11ba0a46: TOKYO: The Japanese economy grew faster than initially thought in the second quarter, revised data showed on Tuesday, ahead of an expected interest rate hike next week.
The world's fourth-largest economy expanded 0.4% in the three months to June, the Cabinet Office said, compared with the 0.3% shown in preliminary data.
Analysts had suggested the initial reading could complicate the Bank of Japan's attempts to lift interest rates as it battles surging inflation and a weaker yen.

The revised data showed private consumption and corporate investment remained weak but better than preliminary data had suggested, but imports came in below the previous estimate, contributing to the upward GDP revision.
The Bank of Japan is expected to hike its key interest rate next week, while prime minister Sanae Takaichi reportedly plans to reshuffle her cabinet, although no major changes are expected.
The yen has come under pressure from elevated oil import costs and concerns about Takaichi's spending plans.
But has been boosted this month by rate hike talk, and is heading towards its highest level this year.
US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent's comment to central bank governor Kazuo Ueda that he supports "Japan's decisive market and monetary steps" has also helped support the currency.
882a5e5836582ac2: NEW YORK, Sept 8 — Zheng Qinwen pulled off another US Open stunner yesterday, rallying to beat Iga Swiatek and reach the quarter-finals as Elena Rybakina and Coco Gauff advanced.
It was one more gritty win for Zheng, the Paris Olympics gold medallist and a former world number four now ranked 121st after struggling in the wake of elbow surgery last year.
Zheng had won the last seven games saving a match point as she shocked Madison Keys in her previous match.
After falling behind 5-0 in the first set against six-time Grand Slam champion Swiatek she again reeled off seven straight.
She then broke Swiatek twice in the second set to clinch the win.
Swiatek, who fell to Zheng in the gold medal match in Paris two years ago, left the Arthur Ashe Stadium in tears.
“I guess to come back from 0-5 (Saturday) is not lucky, that’s all I can say,” Zheng said after becoming the first qualifier or lucky loser to beat Swiatek at a Grand Slam.
Zheng said it took her some time to settle in on the cavernous Ashe court, noting it’s been “a long, long time” since she’d been scheduled on a main show court.
“I just focus on point by point,” Zheng said, adding that she was so focused on the rallies that she lost track of the score.
Zheng is the first qualifier to reach the US Open women’s quarter-finals since Emma Raducanu — who went on to win the title — in 2021.
She’ll next face world number two Rybakina, the reigning Australian Open champion who cruised past a hurting Naomi Osaka 6-1, 6-4 in just 66 minutes.

Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan returns a shot against Naomi Osaka of Japan during their Women’s Singles Fourth Round match on Day Nine of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in the Flushing neighbourhood of the Queens borough of New York City September 7, 2026. — Patrick Smith/Getty Images North America/Getty Images pic via AFP

Rybakina is not only chasing a third Grand Slam title. If she beats Zheng to reach the semi-finals she will seize the number one ranking from Aryna Sabalenka — even if the Belarusian wins a third straight crown.
“Of course I want it,” Rybakina said. “I don’t know anyone who wouldn’t wish this.”
But, she added: “I try to approach the same, fight to the end my next match — let’s see what will happen.”
Fourth-seeded Coco Gauff reached the quarter-finals for the first time since she won the title in 2023, beating 18-year-old US compatriot Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-4.
Gauff next faces fifth-seeded French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, a 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 winner over Anastasia Potapova.

An injury to Potapova in the final game marred an entertaining contest. When Potapova crashed to the ground lunging for a ball Andreeva rushed to her side. The Russian-born Austrian received treatment on her knee before limping to the finish line.

Alexander Blockx’s dream debut continued with a gritty 6-3, 4-6, 7-5, 7-5 victory over Argentina’s Francisco Cerundolo, which made the 21-year-old the first Belgian man to reach the US open last eight.
Blockx, who started the year ranked outside the top 100, said he was “close to retiring” because of sharp pain in an injured rib in the first set.
“Even before the match I was already under medication, and during the match I had medication. So if you feel that much pain while having a lot of medication, that’s not a good sign,” he said.
Men’s top seed Alexander Zverev was once again slated to close the action on Ashe, taking on 21st-seeded Italian Luciano Darderi.
The French Open champion has become a late-night fixture, playing into the small hours not only in two five-set marathons but also in his three-set third round win over Alejandro Tabilo.
The German is vying to make the US Open quarter-finals for a fifth time while Darderi will make the last eight of a Grand Slam for the first time if he can pull off the biggest win of his career.
France’s Arthur Gea was vying for a slice of Grand Slam history against Botic van de Zandschulp. He could become the first men’s lucky loser ever to reach the quarter-finals at a Grand Slam. — AFP
26d8f43afa0512f0: IPOH: Police arrested three people, including a woman, yesterday for their alleged involvement in the theft of production materials from a factory in the Pulai Jaya Industrial Area.

District police chief assistant commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police had received a report on the theft of high-value production materials from the factory, with about 64 rolls reported missing and losses estimated at RM355,000.
"Police subsequently arrested three company employees, aged between 28 and 35, to assist in the investigation," he said when met at the police dinner with media practitioners last night.
Najib said police had also identified another person believed to be linked to the case.

8d87370d1bb696ef: PUTRAJAYA: Asean needs to review the mechanisms for dealing with transboundary haze to prevent adverse impacts on the people's health, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said today.
He said Asean ministers should pay serious attention to the matter as haze could have a direct impact on the health and lives of people, especially children and babies.

"There is room for improvement. I think the Asean ministers must look seriously at it, because this is affecting lives, particularly of children and babies, and if we have seen in Serian, (it) is really concerning," he told reporters after attending a meeting with plantation and commodities ministry staff members here.
The air quality in Serian returned to the hazardous level this morning, with an air pollutant index reading of 302 recorded at the district police headquarters.
Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim declared a haze emergency in Serian last Friday, which was lifted yesterday.
Anwar said the issue of open burning in Indonesia should be thoroughly investigated, including identifying the real cause of the fire before any action or accusations are made.

Asked if there were Malaysian companies operating in the republic that had committed wrongdoings that contributed to the haze, Anwar said the country would respect any legal action by the Indonesian authorities.
"If there are Malaysian companies that are affected (involved), we will give Indonesia space to take action. We will certainly respect the actions there and we will not defend (them)," he said.
He added that Malaysia would not intervene or protect any company if investigations prove they are responsible for open burning or other violations of the law in neighbouring countries.
1dfc1d9c1f6c8513: BEIJING: China began collecting "deposits" on imports of a key chipmaking chemical from Japan on Tuesday after it said a probe found evidence of dumping that harmed Beijing's domestic industry.
The Chinese commerce ministry announced in January an anti-dumping investigation into dichlorosilane imported from Japan - a major global supplier of the chemical used to manufacture semiconductors.

The probe came at a time of heightened diplomatic tensions between the Asian giants after Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi suggested Tokyo may intervene in an attack on the island of Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its territory.

The Chinese commerce ministry said on Monday that "preliminary evidence showed the investigated imports from Japan were involved in dumping, and the domestic dichlorosilane industry suffered substantial damage".
As a result, the ministry said it would implement "temporary anti-dumping measures in the form of a security deposit" beginning Tuesday.
Japanese firms must pay the extra fee, calculated using an assigned deposit collection rate, to China's customs authority.
All Japanese firms are subject to a rate of 99.2%, with the exception of Tokyo-based Denal Silane, which was given a rate of 80.8%.
A spokesman for Japanese chemical conglomerate Shin-Etsu Chemical told AFP the firm was studying the measure.
He declined to discuss financial details about the exports of the product, but said "it represents a very small portion of our business (and) should have no material impact on our overall business".
Minoru Kihara, the Japanese government's chief cabinet secretary, told his daily media briefing that Tokyo would "appropriately respond to China's export control measures".
"Japan has lodged a strong protest and is formally requesting that these measures be withdrawn," he added.
The Chinese commerce ministry did not say how long the imported chemical would be subject to deposits, or when it would announce a final ruling.
258a9ad2b8fb6598: BRUSSELS, Sept 8 — French President Emmanuel Macron has asked European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to deliver a “European legislative text” to ban children aged under 15 from social media to “protect all children in the Union”, according to a letter seen by AFP yesterday.

bdd16e1237a793e2: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim menegaskan kerjasama dan muafakat anggota Jemaah Menteri di tahap baik, walaupun timbul dakwaan sebaliknya.

641e9af0da77a02f: PANAMA CITY, Sept 8 — The number of ships sailing through the Panama Canal could be cut further due to drought caused by the El Nino weather pattern, the new administrator of the waterway told AFP yesterday.
Panama has declared a nationwide emergency over El Nino, a phenomenon developing over the Pacific Ocean that is affecting worldwide weather patterns and pushing up global temperatures.
This year’s El Nino is expected to be the strongest since record-keeping began four decades ago.

Panama’s restrictions come even as use of the canal has risen: shippers are seeking an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blocked in retaliation for the war launched by the United States and Israel.

The interoceanic Panama Canal — which handles five per cent of global maritime trade — has already reduced the maximum number of ships allowed through daily, from 36 last month to 32 by mid-September.
It operates using rainwater that collects in two reservoirs, whose levels have dropped due to the onset of El Nino.
Without water, the locks that lift and lower ships at the start and end of their crossing cannot function.
Ilya Espino de Marotta, who took over as head of the Panama Canal Authority on Monday, told AFP that further measures may be implemented if the drought does not subside.
“We do not rule out the possibility that in February or March we may have to lower the limit — probably not to 24 slots per day, but it could be reduced to 29 or something similar,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The container ship CMA CGM Arctic, sailing under the Maltese flag, passes through the Cocoli Locks of the Panama Canal in Panama City on September 3, 2026, ahead of reduced transit measures linked to the El Nino weather phenomenon that are set to come into force on September 4. — AFP pic
200 million litres per ship
Each ship requires about 200 million litres of water, which is then discharged into the sea.
In 2023, El Nino forced a reduction in daily transits from 38 to 22 due to the dramatic reduction in reservoir levels.
Espino de Marotta, the first woman ever to head the US-built canal authority, stated, however, that she does not expect restrictions to reach the levels seen that year.
Apart from reducing the number of vessels, canal authorities have also reduced their maximum draft, from 15.2 meters to 14.6 meters.
The draft is the vertical distance between the waterline and the lowest point of a ship’s hull. It is a measure of how much water is needed for a ship to float safely without running aground.
Experts have warned that long-term restrictions on canal crossings could lead to higher shipping costs and longer waiting times for deliveries.
The United States and China are the main users of the canal, which is the fastest maritime route between the east coast of the United States and China.
The canal connecting the Atlantic and Pacific handles around 40 per cent of US container traffic.
The Iran war has pushed up traffic through the channel.
With shipping at a standstill in the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for a fifth of the world’s oil and gas, the Panama Canal has become a fallback route for energy shipments. — AFP
6ed149fc0275c9ae: KUALA LUMPUR: The future of Malay and Bumiputera education should not depend on quotas, but on building the capabilities needed to produce knowledge creators, technology owners and economic leaders, says higher education minister Zambry Abd Kadir.

Zambry said educational success should no longer be measured simply by the number of Malay and Bumiputera students entering university, but by their ability to master STEM, develop technology, own intellectual property and build globally competitive companies.

"To achieve this, we need to move from access to quality, from qualifications to competencies, from employment to entrepreneurship, and from using technology to owning technology," he said in his speech at the 2026 Malay Education Convention at the Putra World Trade Centre.
Zambry said universities should not merely produce graduates with degrees, but individuals equipped with knowledge, skills, integrity and the ability to solve problems.

He said higher education issues must also be addressed at their roots, noting the effects of the urban-rural divide, household income and access to technology on a person’s ability to benefit from the economy of the future.
Zambry also said that artificial intelligence (AI) could be a "great equaliser" or a "great divider", depending on students' foundations.
"Students with a strong foundation of knowledge will use AI to think further. Those with a weak foundation may use it to avoid thinking.
"We cannot allow AI to replace the processes of reading, writing, calculating and reasoning. We need to produce people who are empowered by AI, not people who are entirely dependent on AI," he said.

He said Bumiputera youths should be trained to become engineers, researchers, inventors, patent holders, company founders and industry leaders rather than mere operators of technology owned by others.
On language, he said Bahasa Melayu should be strengthened as a language of knowledge, identity and civilisation, while English and other languages should serve as bridges to the wider world.

The convention featured three main discussion sessions: the educational challenges facing children from the B40 and M40 income groups, the role of Universiti Teknologi Mara, and proposed reforms to the Universities and University Colleges Act.
Zambry said the outcomes would be compiled into a resolution to be submitted to deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

a4f03061732212a5: ROSH HAAYIN (Israel), Sept 8 — Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accused the sitting premier of looking merely after his own political survival and not the country’s security, at a rally in central Israel yesterday.

Unveiling the candidates of the Yashar party for the October 27 election, the former military commander said nothing about how he would handle the Palestinian question or the wars against Iran and Lebanon launched by Netanyahu, but accused him of ducking responsibility in the nearly three years since the massive Hamas attack.

A relative newcomer to politics, his party Yashar (Hebrew for “Upright”), founded a year ago, has surged in the polls in recent months, with many voters seeing him as a viable candidate to replace Netanyahu, thanks to a solid military background.

At yesterday’s rally in a hall in the central Israeli city of Rosh Haayin, Eisenkot vowed to put an end to the divisions that have plagued the country since October 7, 2023 over Netanyahu’s conduct of the war in Gaza, where dozens of Israeli hostages were held, and on other fronts.

“In the face of the great rift that opened on October 7, and in the face of the immense challenges before the State of Israel, I believe we need a leadership that knows how to rise to the magnitude of the hour, that knows how to unite and bring unity around what we share, and to fundamentally restore the principles of stateliness and Zionism,” Eisenkot said.
According to a poll by Israel’s public broadcaster Kan published Sunday, Yashar is expected to win 23 Knesset seats out of 120, slightly ahead of Netanyahu’s Likud on 20.

The anti-Netanyahu bloc is projected to win 51 seats, while Netanyahu’s Likud and its coalition partners are polling at 52 in total. ca6cfa0c2eefbacb: JAKARTA: Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta dan dua lagi lapangan terbang di Indonesia kembali beroperasi awal Selasa, selepas pihak berkuasa mengisytiharkan keadaan selamat, sekali gus menamatkan penutupan akibat abu gunung berapi Anak Krakatau sejak kelmarin.

Anak Krakatau meletus tiga kali pagi Selasa, ketika pihak berkuasa Indonesia terus memantau aktiviti gunung berapi itu.

30eb1f365e1a0255: MOSCOW: Russia's defence ministry wants to claim back part of a one-off payout from contract service personnel found guilty of criminal offences at home, a document showed, amid increasing cases of domestic violence among those fighting Russia's war on Ukraine.

Russia provides a minimum one-off payment of 400,000 roubles (US$4,640) for soldiers signing at least a one-year contract to fight in the war with Ukraine that Moscow calls "a special military operation". Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.

In practice, one-off payouts may reach a few million roubles per soldier, depending on the region, in addition to a monthly salary. Russia is also reducing sentences for those serving time in prison in exchange for signing up for the war, among other benefits, as it seeks to bolster army numbers.

Russia has seen a rise in domestic violence as fighters return home for leave, and the defence ministry wants to claim part of the one-off payments "in order to increase the motivation of military personnel to comply with the law", in case of a criminal offence, a draft law published on Monday showed.

If active contract service members are found guilty of a criminal offence which does not imply a prison sentence, they should pay back a portion of the one-off payout based on the months of the service left, the document showed.

Russia does not disclose official statistics on domestic violence committed by its service personnel but independent media, citing military courts data, reported hundreds of such cases, including murders, since the start of the 2022 invasion.

049b62f7dcfcedd5: Huawei has launched a new processor it claims is free of US technology and is using it to drive a new three-screen folding phone. The Chinese giant dubbed the new processor the Kirin 950 Pro and says its LinxiCore processor cores, GPU, and neural processing unit all feature its own designs. The SoC into which Huawei added them uses the "Tau Scaling” architecture that Huawei says arranges components closer to each other to reduce die size and improve performance without needing the kind of advanced chipmaking processes practiced by TSMC and Intel. As The Register wrote when Huawei announced Tau Scaling last May, analysts think Huawei has done interesting things with its silicon but don’t think the company has made any breakthroughs. Huawei begs to differ and says its new silicon offers 42 percent higher performance than the chip it used in the three-screen phone it delivered last year. The Chinese company uses the Kirin 950 Pro in its new three-screen phone, the $2,979 Mate XT2. Analyst firm Counterpoint thinks Huawei will exit 2026 with 24 percent of the total folding phone market, which it believes accounted for 1.6 percent of smartphone sales last year. Huawei therefore has itself a chip that targets the high end of a market niche – and announced it a couple of days before pundits believe Apple will debut a folding iPhone that Counterpoint predicts will win 25 percent of the folding phone market by the end of the year. Huawei’s Kirin 950 Pro will therefore hardly make a dent in the smartphone market. At its launch event, Huawei execs pointed to its totally-not-Android versions of HarmonyOS now running on 85 million devices. That’s strong uptake since Huawei delivered the OS in October 2024. Again, however, it is a fraction of the overall smartphone and smart device market. If Huawei can use the tech it created for the Kirin 950 Pro in other roles that would allow mean Chinese to avoid comparable products from AMD, Intel, or Nvidia, its new chip will show that Chinese firms can create tech that reduces the nation’s reliance on imports. But amid all the hoopla of a phone launch, Huawei hasn’t said anything about its intentions to adapt its new chip for different roles. The Tau Scaling architecture is therefore not going to upset Huawei’s rivals for some time, although western chipmakers do know that Beijing is steering local buyers away from their products and encouraging adoption of local alternatives. Whether any of those Chinese chipmakers succeed beyond the Middle Kingdom is the wider question. China emphasizes export of consumer products as a tactic to fuel domestic growth, and its smartphone makers Xiaomi, Oppo, and Honor have delivered on that mission by winning solid sales across Europe, Africa, and Latin America – with phones running Android and tied to Google services. Huawei’s hardware and HarmonyOS ecosystem, by contrast, have not racked up notable success outside China. ®

423c54356f72b7db: IPOH, Sept 8 — No land acquisition involving individual landowners has been carried out so far for the RM6.25 billion Ipoh Sentral development project, the Perak Legislative Assembly was told today.

Saarani was replying to a supplementary question from Buntong assemblyman Thulsi Manogaran, who asked whether the project would involve the acquisition of privately owned land, resulting in property owners having to relocate.

From the tourism and services perspective, Saarani said the expected increase in domestic and international tourist arrivals through Ipoh Sentral would bring direct economic spillover benefits to Buntong and Perak as a whole.

b840bf675db01a51: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Malaysian Organisation of Vape Entity (MOVE) has called for urgent legal and regulatory clarity following a High Court ruling that nullified the 2023 exemption of liquid nicotine from the Poisons List.

The industry group, which represents more than 55,000 members, said the government’s decision not to pursue an appeal against the ruling had created legal uncertainty that could push consumers towards an illicit vaping market.

MOVE president Samsul K. Arrifin said the government should reconcile the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 (Act 852) with the Poisons Act to establish a clear and consistent regulatory framework.

“Malaysia has already taken an important step by enacting the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 (Act 852). What is needed now is clarity and consistency in how the law is implemented. A regulatory outcome that removes compliant businesses without addressing existing demand could simply push that demand into an unregulated market,” he said in a statement.
MOVE said its main concern was that a prohibition-driven outcome could undermine safeguards intended to protect consumers and young people.
It said registered retailers could be subjected to age-verification requirements, standard operating procedures and enforcement oversight, unlike illicit sellers operating outside those controls.

The group also warned that an unregulated market could increase the risk of products containing unknown ingredients or tampered liquids, while making it harder for authorities to enforce product standards, traceability requirements and tax collection.

“Prohibition does not automatically remove demand. It removes the regulated channel. If the objective is to protect youth and consumers, the stronger approach is to keep the market visible, accountable and enforceable,” Samsul said.

MOVE said Act 852 should remain the regulatory blueprint and urged the government and Health Ministry to provide immediate legal clarity, regulate rather than prohibit vaping products, and empower compliant retailers to act as gatekeepers against sales to minors.

It called for strict requirements covering product safety, traceability, ingredient transparency and age verification, as well as standardised identity checks and operating procedures for registered businesses.

MOVE said it was ready to engage with the government and relevant authorities on a controlled, data-driven regulatory approach focused on youth protection, consumer safety, product accountability and enforcement.

e6f459c52030cd8c: WASHINGTON, Sept 8 — President Donald Trump threatened yesterday to block US sales of Canadian plane maker Bombardier unless it builds aircrafts in the country, complaining of “unjust and unfair” bilateral trade provisions as he escalates a tariff war.

The angry social media post marks the second stunning potential move by the US leader this year against the manufacturer, which has thousands of its aircraft currently operating in US airlines’ domestic fleets.
And it comes on the eve of Canada imposing retaliatory tariffs on a range of US goods beginning today.
“No more selling Bombardier in the United States!” Trump posted in all caps on his Truth Social platform, although he did not specify how he would achieve a sales halt.
“If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ‘piggybank.’”
“Canada blocks our GREAT American Banks, and Companies” from doing business there, Trump added. “That Era is OVER!”
The US market accounts for more than half of Bombardier’s revenue, Trump said.

Back in January, furious over what he said was Canada’s refusal to grant certification to new models of US-made Gulfstream jets, the president threatened to decertify Bombardier planes in the United States and impose a 50-per cent tariff on Canadian aircraft.
Those threats apparently were never carried out, but Trump said Canada quickly certified Gulfstream planes the following month because of his intervention.
Trump’s social media post yesterday signaled continued acrimony over Bombardier, amid a broiling bilateral tariff fight.

Even if Trump sought to follow through on his latest threat, it remained unclear how it would happen. The Federal Aviation Administration, not the White House, is the US agency that certifies or decertifies aircraft in the country.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This photograph shows a Bombardier Dash 8 Q400 MR aircraft dropping fire retardant over a forest fire near Puilaurens, south-western France September 5, 2026. — AFP pic
Bombardier models remain US certified and the company is currently exempt from US tariffs. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment about Trump’s post.
Last month, as trade negotiations collapsed, Trump slapped 50-per cent tariffs on some US$20 billion worth of Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to cement.
Canada announced it is imposing retaliatory tariffs on a similar amount of US products beginning early Tuesday.
The duties of 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent will apply to imports from the United States covering steel and aluminum products as well as dairy goods like cheese.
Negotiations between the two sides broke down late last month after days of meetings in Washington, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney saying he decided to suspend the trade talks.

At the time, Carney said the Trump administration’s terms were ultimately unacceptable, and that US negotiators had introduced restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries at the eleventh hour.
US officials also made unacceptable “threats” to the French language and “Quebec culture,” he added, referencing the French-speaking province in eastern Canada.
Ottawa and Washington have not resumed negotiations since, and have continued trading barbs. — AFP
9df2a000d362ff4f: Baru-baru ini saya menonton kembali filem Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang arahan Mamat Khalid. Kali pertama saya menontonnya ialah ketika filem itu ditayangkan di pawagam. Saya tak ingat tahun berapa sehinggalah selepas disemak kembali, rupanya pada 2008. Maknanya sudah hampir dua dekad.

Entah kenapa filem ini sedikit tenggelam apabila orang bercakap tentang karya Mamat Khalid. Kita lebih mudah mengingati Rock, Zombi Kampung Pisang, Hantu Kak Limah dan segala macam watak serta dialog daripada filem-filemnya yang sudah masuk dalam budaya popular sedangkan Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang pun sedap juga.

Setelah menontonnya kembali hampir 20 tahun kemudian, saya rasa filem ini memberitahu sesuatu tentang Mamat Khalid yang kelihatannya terlindung di sebalik reputasi beliau sebagai pengarah komedi -- mamat ini sangat faham bahasa sinema.

Ironinya, Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang bukanlah filem yang tidak dihargai ketika zamannya. Pada Festival Filem Malaysia ke-21 (2008), filem ini memenangi Filem Terbaik, Pengarah Terbaik untuk Mamat Khalid dan Pelakon Lelaki Terbaik menerusi Rosyam Nor, selain Penataan Seni Terbaik dan Pereka Kostum/Busana Terbaik. Pada Anugerah Skrin tahun yang sama, ia turut memenangi Filem Terbaik, Pengarah Terbaik dan Pelakon Lelaki Terbaik.

Jadi ini bukan perihal filem yang gagal kemudian kita sengaja mahu angkat semula. Tak! Ia pernah diraikan. Cuma entah bagaimana, apabila masa berlalu dan nama Mamat Khalid semakin besar, filem ini seperti tersorok sedikit di belakang karya-karya beliau yang lain. Mungkin kerana Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang agak aneh. Atau penonton kita jarang didedahkan dengan konsep komedi yang pelbagai dalam filem Melayu, malah kita pun tak begitu mahir yang komedi ada banyak cabang.

Yang kita selalu nampak, 'kelakar' hanyalah gelak ketawa dengan dialog, aksi serta mimik wajah yang bersekali. Kita tak tahu komedi ada 'slapstick', situation comedy (sitcom), 'deadpan', dark comedy dan satu dua lagi. Apatah lagi konsep 'noir' dalam filem Melayu yang memang asing.

Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang -- filem yang dibuat dalam hitam putih ini membawa kita ke sebuah pekan pada zaman 1950-an bersama Saleh (lakonan Rosyam Nor), seorang wartawan yang terjebak dalam satu misteri. Ada pembunuhan, watak-watak misteri, jembalang dan harimau jadian, orang-orang pelik dan suasana yang kadang-kadang membuatkan kita tidak pasti sama ada Mamat sedang serius atau sedang mengenakan kita. Rupanya kedua-duanya.

Malah ada beberapa babak membuat saya ketawa lebih panjang berbanding saya menonton filem-filem komedi lain karya beliau terutama bila mendengarkan 'voice over' Saleh; ketika dia mengejar seseorang, kerap dia merungut tentang kesukaran dia berlari laju kerana penyakit angin pasang yang dihidapinya.

Pada permukaannya kita boleh mengatakan Mamat sedang bermain dengan filem noir, genre yang kita kenal melalui filem detektif lama Hollywood -- permainan cahaya dan bayang. Tetapi Mamat tidak sekadar meminjam teknik Hollywood. Dia mencampurkannya dengan suasana filem Melayu studio zaman dahulu dengan mengadunkan unsur seram, melodrama dan perangai orang kita sendiri.

Sebab itu saya kata Mamat faham bahasa sinema dan budaya sendiri. Ada beberapa babak dia 'membantai' perangai orang kita. Karyawan yang mahu bermain dan melanggar sesuatu genre terlebih dahulu perlulah memahami genre yang hendak dipersendakannya. Maka itu, adunan kesemua resipi itu mencipta satu identiti iaitu 'filem Mamat Khalid'. Hitam putihnya bukan sekadar supaya nampak klasik. Kostum, bangunan, kedai, kenderaan, cahaya, muzik, cara manusia berdiri malah cara mereka bercakap semuanya membantu membina sebuah dunia. Kita boleh mengambil satu babak tanpa mengetahui tajuk filemnya dan rasanya tetap ada cap dagang Mamat pada gambar itu. Ini sisi Mamat yang kadang-kadang tenggelam kerana kita terlalu mengingatinya melalui lawak.

Dalam Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang, perkara itu jelas. Ia filem misteri, komedi, seram, parodi dan satira dalam satu masa. Saya pernah baca, ada pengkaji dan pengkritik filem mentafsir lebih jauh sindiran politik dan sosial di dalamnya, termasuk simbol-simbol tertentu seperti bulan dan keris yang dikaitkan dengan kuasa, masyarakat serta industri filem sendiri. Mamat juga melalui dialog Saleh, selamba menyentuh tentang perjuangan komunis yang sia-sia dan tidak mendapat tempat di Malaysia.

Saya tidak mahu pergi sejauh itu. Kalau semua benda hendak dicari simbolnya, nanti tengok keris kita takut, tengok bulan kita gelabah, macam kita fobia dengan simbol mata dan segi tiga. Tetapi memang terasa Mamat menggunakan dunia lama untuk bercakap tentang dunia semasanya. Semuanya dimasukkan ke dalam dunia pelik yang dibinanya. Bagi mereka yang selalu menyangka filem adalah dunia realiti, pasti akan menemui kepayahan jika menonton filem ini.

Saya juga pernah terbaca yang Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang agak berserabut dan terlalu banyak perkara mahu dimasukkan. Ada pengkritik juga melihat, apabila cerita semakin berkembang, ia mula melemah dan kurang meyakinkan seperti bagaimana permulaan ceritanya. Akibatnya, keghairahan untuk menonton sampai habis pun mengendur. Tetapi setelah menontonnya kembali baru-baru ini, saya boleh pula meleraikan keserabutan itu. Ini kerana ada pengkritik filem juga pernah berkata, kita tak semestinya perlu memahami cerita sesebuah filem itu sekiranya kita seronok menontonnya. Cukup kita menikmatinya sahaja. Saya setuju. Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang adalah filem yang cukup sekadar kita nikmatinya, tak payah susah-susah memahaminya. Cuma, apa yang boleh saya kata ialah Mamat Khalid adalah genius sinema.

Selepas pemergiannya pada 2021, kita semakin sedar betapa banyak watak dan dialog ciptaannya sudah menjadi sebahagian budaya popular. Orang masih menyebut Kampung Pisang. Orang masih mengulang dialog Hantu Kak Limah. Watak daripada dunia Rock masih dikenali. Man Laksa dirindukan. Itu pencapaian besar seorang pembikin filem. Mamat Khalid berjaya mengubah suatu kebiasaan. Orang masuk panggung mahu tonton cerita yang dibuat Mamat Khalid, bukan sangat hendak melihat muka-muka yang kacak lawa. Mamat Khalid berjaya mempopularkan pelakon-pelakon 'muka awam' (istilah orang sekarang) dalam filem-filem yang selalu menjadi sebutan ramai itu.

Cuma sesekali elok juga kita berjalan keluar sedikit dari Kampung Pisang untuk melihat karya Mamat yang ini. Di dalam Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang, kita mungkin akan bertemu Mamat Khalid yang sedikit berbeza daripada yang selalu kita kenang. Ini Mamat yang menunjukkan bahawa di sebalik segala lawaknya, dia seorang pencinta filem yang tahu bagaimana gambar, cahaya, bunyi, ruang, watak dan genre boleh digunakan untuk bercerita. Mamat telah membuktikan betapa luasnya dunia sinema untuk dipelbagaikan dalam sesebuah karya.

Filem Kala Malam Bulan Mengambang seperti sengaja dibuat hitam putih oleh Mamat supaya kelihatan seperti sebuah filem lama. Dan kini setelah hampir dua dekad, ia benar-benar menjadi sebuah filem lama. Pernah diiktiraf dengan anugerah tetapi ternyata ia telah dilupakan. Itu ironinya. Entah-entah memang ironi ini telah dijangka oleh Mamat. Agaknyalah! Kalau benar -- saya suka ironi ini.

a7697c4dfda2d66c: From Terence Netto
For nearly two decades now Abdul Rahman Kassim of PAS has been striving to better ties between his party and Christian groups in the north of the Peninsula.
His efforts have taken the form of organising dialogue sessions between his party’s leaders and priests and lay activists of mainly the Catholic Church in northern Perak, Kedah and Penang.

When Sebastian Francis became Bishop of Penang in 2013, Rahman found in the bishop, who was elevated to the office of cardinal in 2023, a ready interlocutor between Islamists like him and the Catholic Church.

Get-to-know-you sessions, dialogues, high teas, lunches, dinners and visits to architecturally interesting mosques, were organised by Rahman and his cohort for the edification of their Catholic counterparts.
Sebastian and his entourage, which included on occasion this scribe, were, at times, transfixed by the hospitality and goodwill exuded by their hosts.
With the vibes that good, Christian-Muslim relations appeared to be a cinch, but this reporter was sceptical because their theologies clashed on several fronts, too stark to ignore.
But Rahman, an optimist who declines to dwell on the problematic, is unfazed by these contradictions.
Once he even invited Cardinal Sebastian to grace his daughter’s wedding held at his home in Tasek Gelugor, Penang.

The prelate accepted the invitation, mingling and talking with Rahman’s guests during dinner, causing no small amount of surprise and delight among people unused to seeing a crucifix-wearing personage of the church at ease in their midst.

A PAS activist of more than four decades’ involvement, 70-year-old Rahman has shown no interest in scaling the party hierarchy which is probably why his colleagues view his exertions in promoting Muslim-Christian ties as something to be welcomed.
Rahman also knows that Sebastian is due for retirement at the end of this year when he reaches the church’s mandatory retirement age of 75.
Rahman had set, as a goal of his two decade-long effort at outreach to Christians, the cardinal’s acceptance of an invitation to attend the 72nd muktamar in Kota Bharu.

He wasn’t sure Sebastian would accept the invitation knowing that though the prelate’s jurisdiction as Bishop of Penang included Kelantan, he is too busy with church matters to find time for non-ecclesiastical affairs.

Rahman was besides himself with joy when Sebastian called him on Thursday morning from Penang airport to say he is coming to the muktamar, being held at Dewan Putik, near the airport in Pengkalan Chepa.
In the event, the cardinal’s attendance was a landmark in that it was the first time in annual general meetings of the Islamic party that a high-ranking Catholic prelate graced the occasion.
The cardinal’s amiable and unassuming ways, familiar to Rahman, smoothed the introductions to the crowd of PAS grandees who were pleasantly surprised by his presence.
It has been Sebastian’s position that familiarity with PAS higher-ups was necessary so that should problems arise where and whenever PAS rules, communication would not be a problem.
Thus the cardinal has positioned himself and the Church in prescient anticipation.
Terence Netto is a senior journalist and an FMT reader.

f1e3b4a2a08906cf: "I cannot."
With those two words, a golf club security manager laid bare a problem that haunts every courtroom, every tender and every audit in Malaysia.

S Saravanan, group security head of Tropicana Golf & Country Resort, was testifying on Sept 1 in the corruption trial of former prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin. The club's computer records showed Muhyiddin had played golf with businessman Azman Yusoff on July 19, 2020, a date that matters to the case.

Then came the cross-examination. Could he vouch for the accuracy of the information in the system? "I cannot," he admitted. When defence counsel pressed that "it can be modified", the best Saravanan could offer was "I am not sure about that".
And just like that, the record wobbled. Not because anyone proved tampering, but because nobody could prove there was none.

This is not one trial's problem. On Aug 27, Malaysians witnessed a spectacle no country would envy: three former prime ministers, Najib Razak, Muhyiddin Yassin and Ismail Sabri Yaakob, at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex on the same day for separate proceedings.

Najib faced a US$5.64 billion (RM22.8 billion) civil suit brought by 1MDB; Muhyiddin's trial over charges of soliciting RM225.3 million in bribes for Bersatu continued, charges he is contesting; and Ismail Sabri pleaded not guilty to failing to declare assets to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). The courts will decide each case on their merits.

But every one of these cases turns on records. Bank statements, procurement papers, approval chains, logbooks. And the first move of any defence is to ask the same devastating question: how do you know this record was not changed?

It is a fair question. Almost every record the Malaysian state relies on, from tender evaluations in ePerolehan, the finance ministry's e-procurement system, to departmental expenditure files, lives in an ordinary database.
An ordinary database can be edited by whoever holds the administrator password. History, in other words, belongs to whoever controls the server.

Here is where blockchain technology can earn its keep. Not the meme-coin casino that has soured many on the word, but something far more boring and far more useful: a public logbook that nobody, not even the government, can rewrite.

The mechanics are simple. Every time a record is created - a bid submitted, a score entered, an award signed - the system generates its cryptographic hash, a unique digital fingerprint, and publishes that fingerprint to a blockchain. The record itself stays private; only the fingerprint goes public.
If anyone later alters so much as a comma, the fingerprint no longer matches. Tampering does not become impossible. It becomes instantly detectable, by anyone, forever.

Let me be honest about what this cannot do. A blockchain cannot verify that a record was true when it was written; log the wrong 15 names and the wrong 15 names are preserved for eternity. Nor will it stop cash in envelopes or phone calls that never touch a system.

But look at what it kills: backdating, quiet edits, vanishing files, doctored evaluations. The cover-up, in short. In court, it transforms the question from "can this record be trusted?", which no witness can answer, into "has this record changed since the day it was made?", which mathematics answers.

This is not theory. Estonia became the first country to run blockchain in live government systems in 2012, and today its land registry, business registry, state gazette and more than a million health records are anchored this way.

The World Economic Forum and the Inter-American Development Bank have trialled a blockchain procurement system for Colombia's school meals programme, complete with automatic red flags for suspicious bids.

Malaysia does not even need to build the rails. The Malaysia Blockchain Infrastructure, developed by national research agency MIMOS Berhad with MY EG Services and powered by the Zetrix chain, has been operational since April 2025. What is missing is the mandate. Three moves would supply it.

First, anchor procurement. The finance ministry should require ePerolehan to hash every tender milestone, submission, evaluation score and award decision to the national blockchain the moment each occurs.

Azam Baki, in his final days as MACC chief commissioner this May, put procurement and public fund leakages at an estimated RM277 billion over six years, warning: "We cannot afford to slow down. Corruption in this country is still serious and in certain sectors it is systemic."

Second, wire in the Auditor-General. Give the National Audit Department live, read-only access to anchored expenditure logs, turning audits from post-mortems into continuous monitoring. The Auditor-General's first report for 2026 flagged 273 new financial and governance issues. Catching them as they happen beats cataloguing them years later.

Third, update the Evidence Act 1950. Section 90A admits computer records on a certificate that were produced in the course of ordinary use, a presumption any sharp lawyer can shake, as Tuesday showed. A cryptographic proof of integrity should stand alongside it, so court time is spent arguing the case, not the logbook.

Malaysia's score on Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index rose to 52 this year, lifting us to 54th place and third in Asean. Enforcement is working. But records that cannot be quietly rewritten would harden the entire system by protecting the innocent and cornering the guilty.
No witness should again be left saying "I cannot" while justice hangs on a database. The technology is proven and the losses are counted. What Putrajaya needs now is the will.

c06ee91cce4eead7: Saya ingin membuat sedikit komentar berkenaan kenyataan Setiausaha Agung PAS Takiyuddin Hassan baru-baru ini tentang sokong PAS boleh masuk syurga.
